   121	
   122	\begin{remark}
   123	  \label{rk:higher-level}
   124	  Note that for any integer $\ell\geq 1$ the collection of $\ell$-level CL
   125	  functions trivially contains the collection of $(\ell-1)$-level CL functions:
   126	  for this it suffices to note that the $0$ function, which is a $0$-level CL
   127	  function, is also a $1$-level CL function by setting $V_1=V$, $V_{>1}= \{0\}$,
   128	  $L_1(x)=0$ for all $x\in V$, and $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ is the $0$ map for all
   129	  $x\in V$.
   130	\end{remark}
   131	
   132	\begin{definition}
   133	  \label{def:cl-dist}
   134	  Let $L, R: V \to V$ be conditionally linear functions.
   135	  The \emph{conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L,R}$ corresponding to $(L,
   136	    R)$} is defined as the distribution over pairs $(L(x), R(x)) \in V \times V$
   137	  for $x$ drawn uniformly at random from $V$.
   138	\end{definition}
   139	
   140	Throughout the paper we abbreviate ``conditionally linear functions'' and
   141	``conditionally linear distributions'' as \emph{CL functions} and \emph{CL
   142	  distributions}, respectively.
   143	
   144	The following lemma elucidates structural properties of $\ell$-level CL
   145	functions.
   146	Recall that using our shorthand notation, $x^{L_{<k}}$ and $x^{L_k}$ in the
   147	lemma denote $L_{<k}(x)$ and $L_{k,u}(x^{V_{k,\, u}})$ where $u = L_{<k}(x)$.
   148	
   149	
   150	\begin{lemma}
   151	  \label{lem:cl-kth}
   152		Let $\ell \geq 1$ and $V = \F^n$ for some integer $n \geq 0$.
   153	  A function $L: V \to V$ is an $\ell$-level CL function if and only if the
   154	  following collection of functions and subspaces exists:
   155	  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
   156	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-marginal} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$, a
   157	    function $L_{\le k} : V \to V$ called the \emph{$k$-th marginal of $L$};
   158	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-space} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u
   159	    \in L_{<k} (V)$, a register subspace $V_{k,\, u}$ of $V$ called the
   160	    \emph{$k$-th factor space with prefix $u$};
   161	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-map} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u \in
   162	    L_{<k} (V)$, a linear map $L_{k,\, u} : V_{k,\, u} \to V_{k,\, u}$ called
   163	    the \emph{$k$-th linear map of $L$ with prefix $u$};
   164	  \end{enumerate}
   165	  such that the following conditions hold for all $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots,
   166	  \ell\}$.
   167	  \begin{enumerate}
   168	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-cl} $L_{\leq k}$ is a $k$-level CL function on $V$;
   169		\item \label{enu:cl-space-sum} $V = \bigoplus_{i = 1}^\ell V_{i,\,
   170	      x^{L_{<i}}}$ for all $x \in V$;
   171	\item \label{enu:cl-map-sum} $L_{\leq k}(x) = \sum_{i = 1}^{k} x^{L_i}$ for
   172	    all $x \in V$, where $L_i$ is shorthand notation for $L_{i,\,
   173	      x^{L_{<i}}}$;
   174	  \item \label{enu:cl-last-ell} $L = L_{\leq \ell}$.
   175	  \end{enumerate}
   176	  As in \cref{enu:cl-map-sum}, we sometimes use $V_k$ and $L_k$ to denote
   177	  $V_{k,\, u}$ and $L_{k,\, u}$ respectively, leaving the prefix $u$ implicit.
   178	\end{lemma}
   179	
   180	\begin{proof}
   181		We first prove the ``if'' direction: if there exist spaces and functions
   182	  satisfying the conditions in the lemma, the fact that $L$ is an $\ell$-level
   183	  CL function follows from \cref{enu:cl-k-cl,enu:cl-last-ell} of the lemma
   184	  statement.
   185	
   186	  We now prove the ``only if'' direction.
   187	  Given a CL function $L$ on $V$, we construct the $k$-th family of subspaces
   188	  and functions for all $k \in \{1, \ldots, \ell\}$ by induction on the level
   189	  $\ell$.
   190	  First consider the base case $\ell=1$.
   191	  Since $L_{<1} = 0$, we omit the mentioning of the prefix $u \in L_{<1}(V)$.
   192	  Define $L_{\leq 1} = L$, the factor space $V_1 = V$, and the linear map $L_1 =
   193	  L$.
   194	  It is straightforward to verify that the conditions in the lemma hold for
   195	  these choices of linear maps and spaces.
   196	  
   197	  Now, assume that the lemma holds for CL functions of level at most $\ell - 1$,
   198	  and we prove the lemma for $\ell$-level CL functions.
   199	  By definition, an $\ell$-level CL function $L$ can be written as
   200	  \begin{equation*}
   201	  	L(x) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{V_{>1}})
   202	  \end{equation*}
   203	  for some linear map $L_1 : V_1 \to V_1$ and a family of $(\ell-1)$-level CL
   204	  functions
   205	  \begin{equation*}
   206	    \bigl \{ L_{>1,\, v} : V_{>1} \to V_{>1} \bigr \}_{\, v \in L_1(V_1)}
   207	  \end{equation*}
   208	  where $V_1$ and $V_{>1}$ are complementary register subspaces of $V$.
   209	  Next, using the inductive hypothesis on the $(\ell-1)$-level CL function
   210	  $L_{>1,\, v}$ we get that for all $v \in L_1(V_1)$ and all $k \in \{1, 2,
   211	  \ldots, \ell-1\}$ there exist $k$-th marginal functions $L'_{v,\, \le k}:
   212	  V_{>1} \to V_{>1}$, $k$-th factor spaces $V'_{v,\, k,\, u}$, and $k$-th linear
   213	  maps $L'_{v,\, k,\, u}$ of $L_{>1,\, v}$ with prefix $u \in L'_{v,\,
   214	    <k}(V_{>1})$ such that the conditions of the lemma for $L_{>1,\, v}$ hold.
   215	  
   216	  Define the marginal functions $L_{\le k} : V \to V$, factor spaces
   217	  $V_{k,\, u}$ and linear maps $L_{k,\, u}$ for $L$ as follows.
   218	  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
   219	  \item Define $L_{\le 1} = L_1$ and the first factor space to be $V_1$;
   220	  \item For all $k \in \{2, 3, \ldots, \ell\}$, define
   221	    \begin{equation}
   222	      \label{eq:cl-k-def}
   223	      L_{\le k}: x \mapsto x^{L_1} + L'_{x^{L_1},\, <k} (x^{V_{>1}})
   224	      \quad\text{for } x\in V;
   225	    \end{equation}
   226		\item For all $k \in \{2, 3, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u \in L_{< k}(V)$, define
   227	    $V_{k,\, u} = V'_{v,\, k-1,\, w}$ and $L_{k,\, u} = L'_{v,\, k-1,\, w}$
   228	    where $v = u^{V_1} \in L_{1}(V_{1})$ and $w = u^{V_{>1}} \in L'_{v,< k-1}(V_{> 1})$.
   229	  \end{enumerate}
   230	  We verify that the conditions of the lemma are satisfied.
   231	  Since $L'_{v,\, < k}$ is by assumption a $(k-1)$-level CL function on $V_{>
   232	    1}$, we get that $L_{\leq k}$ is a $k$-level CL function on $V$ from
   233	  \cref{eq:cl-k-def}, establishing \cref{enu:cl-k-cl}.
   234	  By the induction hypothesis, we have for all $v\in L_1(V_1)$ and $y \in
   235	  V_{>1}$,
   236	  \begin{equation}
   237	    \label{eq:cl-k-1}
   238	    V_{>1} = \bigoplus_{i=1}^{\ell-1}
   239	    V'_{\smash{v,\, i, \, y^{L'_{v,\, <i}}}},
   240	  \end{equation}
   241	  which implies that for all $x \in V$ and $v = x^{L_1}$,
   242	  \begin{equation*}
   243	    V = V_1 \oplus \Big ( \bigoplus_{i=1}^{\ell-1}
   244	    V'_{\smash{v,\, i, \, x^{L'_{v,\, <i}}}} \Big)
   245	    = V_1 \oplus \Big (\bigoplus_{i=2}^{\ell} V_{i,\, x^{L_{<i}}} \Big)
   246	    = \bigoplus_{i=1}^\ell V_{i,\, x^{L_{<i}}}\;.
   247	  \end{equation*}
   248	  The first equality follows from \cref{eq:cl-k-1} while the second and third
   249	  equalities follow from the definition of $V_{k,\, u}$.
   250	  This establishes \cref{enu:cl-space-sum}.
   251	
   252	  Next, we have that for all $x \in V$, $v = x^{L_1}$, and $k \in
   253	  \{1,2,\ldots,\ell\}$,
   254	  \begin{align}
   255	    \label{eq:cl-last-ell}
   256	    L_{\leq k}(x)
   257	    & = v + L'_{v,\, <k} (x^{V_{>1}}) \\
   258	    & = v + \sum_{i=1}^{k-1} x^{L'_{v,\, i}}
   259	    = \sum_{i = 1}^{k} x^{L_{i}}, \label{eq:cl-last-ell2}
   260	  \end{align}
   261	  where $L'_{v,\, i}$ is the $i$-th linear map of $L_{>1,\, v}$ with prefix
   262	  $L'_{v,\, <i}(x)$ and $L_i$ is the $i$-th linear map of $L$ with prefix
   263	  $L_{<i}(x)$.
   264	  The second equality follows from the inductive hypothesis applied to $L'_{v,\,
   265	    <k}$ and the third equality follows from the definition of $L_{i}$.
   266	  Line~\eqref{eq:cl-last-ell2} implies \cref{enu:cl-map-sum} of the lemma.
   267	  
   268	  Finally, \Cref{enu:cl-last-ell} follows from~\eqref{eq:cl-last-ell} where we
   269	  set $k = \ell$ and observe that $L'_{x^{L_1},\, \le \ell-1}$ is equal to
   270	  $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ by the inductive hypothesis.
   271	  This shows that $L_{\le k}$, $V_{k,\, u}$, and $L_{k,\, u}$ satisfy the
   272	  conditions of the lemma and completes the induction.
   273	\end{proof}
   274	
   275	We note that the marginal functions, factor spaces, and linear maps of a given
   276	CL function $L$ may not be unique; for example, consider the identity function
   277	on a linear space $V = \F^n$.
   278	This is clearly a $1$-level CL function, but it can also be viewed as a
   279	$k$-level CL function for $k \in \{2, \ldots, n\}$ with an arbitrary partition
   280	of $V$ into factor spaces.
   281	
   282	\begin{lemma}
   283	  \label{lem:cl-concat}
   284	  Let $\ell, k \ge 0$ be integers and $U = \F^n$, $V = \F^m$ be linear spaces.
   285	  Suppose $L$ is a $k$-level CL function on $U$ and $R_u$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   286	  function on $V$ for each $u \in L(U)$.
   287	  Then the \emph{concatenation} $T$ of $L$ and $\{R_u\}_u$ defined as
   288	  \begin{equation*}
   289	    T (x) = L(x^U) + R_{L(x^U)} (x^V)
   290	  \end{equation*}
   291	  is a $(k+\ell)$-level conditionally linear function on $U\oplus V$.
   292	\end{lemma}
   293	
   294	\begin{proof}
   295	  We prove the claim by induction on $k$.
   296	  The case $k = 0$ follows from the Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   297	  Assume that the lemma holds for $L$ being at most $(k-1)$-level.
   298	  By Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}, there are complementary register subspaces
   299	  $U_1$ and $U_{>1}$ of $U$, a linear function $L_1$ on $U_1$, and a family of
   300	  $(k-1)$-level CL functions $L_{>1,\, v}$ for $v \in L_1(U_1)$ such that
   301	  \begin{equation*}
   302	    L(x^U) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}).
   303	  \end{equation*}
   304	  For all $x^{L_1}$, define the function $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ on $U_{>1} \oplus V$ as
   305	  \begin{equation*}
   306	    T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1} \oplus V}) = L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}) +
   307	    R_{x^{L_1} + x^{L_{>1}}}(x^V),
   308	  \end{equation*}
   309	  the concatenation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ and $\{ R_{L(x^U)} \}_{x^{L_{>1}}}$
   310	  where $L_{>1}$ is the shorthand notation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$.
   311	  By the induction hypothesis, $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ is $(k+\ell-1)$-level
   312	  conditionally linear.
   313	  The lemma follows from Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   314	\end{proof}
   315	\begin{lemma}[Direct sums of CL functions]
   316	  \label{lem:cl-func-prod}
   317	  Let $V^{(1)}, V^{(2)}, \ldots, V^{(m)}$ be register subspaces of $V$ such that
   318	  $V = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   319	  Suppose that, for each $j\in\{1, 2, \ldots, m\}$, $L^{(j)}$ is an
   320	  $\ell_j$-level conditionally linear function on $V^{(j)}$.
   321	  Then the direct sum $L = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   322	  function over $V$ for $\ell = \max_j \{\ell_j\}$, where $L$ is defined by
   323	  \begin{equation*}
   324	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m  L^{(j)}(x^{(j)})
   325	  \end{equation*}
   326	  for all $x = \sum_{j=1}^m x^{(j)} \in \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   327	\end{lemma}
   328	
   329	\begin{proof}
   330	  It is easy to see that an $\ell$-level CL function is also $k$-level
   331	  conditionally linear for all $k \ge \ell$.
   332	  Hence, it suffices to prove the claim where $\ell_j = \ell$ for $j=1, 2,
   333	  \ldots, m$.
   334	
   335	  We prove the theorem by an induction on $\ell$.
   336	  For $\ell = 1$, the functions $L^{(j)}$ are linear and the claim follows by
   337	  the fact that the direct sum of linear maps is linear.
   338	
   339	  Assume now the theorem holds for conditionally linear functions of level at
   340	  most $\ell-1$ and $L^{(j)}$ are $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions
   341	  for $j=1, 2, ,\ldots, m$.
   342	  By definition, $L^{(j)}$ is the concatenation of conditionally linear
   343	  functions $L^{(j)}_{1}$ on $V^{(j)}_1$ and $\{ L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j} \}_{v_j}$
   344	  on $V^{(j)}_{>1}$ of levels $1$, and $\ell-1$ respectively.
   345	  Furthermore,
   346	  \begin{equation*}
   347	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)} (x^{(j)}) = \sum_{j=1}^m \Bigl( v_j +
   348	    L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   349	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr) \Bigr),
   350	  \end{equation*}
   351	  where $v_j = L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   352	    \Bigr)$.
   353	  By the induction hypothesis,
   354	  \begin{equation*}
   355	    L_{1} (x^{V_1}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   356	    \Bigr),\quad L_{>1,\, v} (x^{V_{>1}}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   357	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr)
   358	  \end{equation*}
   359	  are $1$-level and $(\ell-1)$-level conditionally linear respectively for $v =
   360	  \sum_j v_j$, $V_1 = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_1$, and $V_{>1} =
   361	  \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_{>1}$.
   362	  This proves that $L$ is $\ell$-level conditionally linear.
   363	\end{proof}
   364	
   365	\begin{lemma}
   366	  \label{lem:cl-dist-prod}
   367	  For each $i \in \{1,\ldots,m\}$ let $L^{(i)}, R^{(i)} : V^{(i)} \to V^{(i)}$
   368	  be $\ell_i$-level conditionally linear functions and let $L, R: V \to V$ be the
   369	  direct sums $L = \bigoplus_i L_i$ and $R = \bigoplus_i R_i$, respectively, as
   370	  defined in Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-func-prod}.
   371	  Then the conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L, R}$ is the product
   372	  distribution $\prod_{i=1}^m \mu_{L^{(i)},\, R^{(i)}}$ over $V \times V$.
   373	\end{lemma}
   374	
   375	\begin{proof}
   376		The distribution $\mu_{L,R}$ is the distribution over pairs $(L(x),R(x))$
   377	  where $x$ is sampled uniformly from $V \times V$.
   378	  By Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-func-prod}, this is equivalent to the distribution over
   379	  pairs $\bigl( (L_i(x^{V_i}))_{i=1}^m, (R_i(x^{V_i}))_{i=1}^m \bigr)$ where $x$
   380	  is chosen uniformly at random from $V$.
   381	  This distribution is exactly the product of the distributions $
   382	  \mu_{L^{(i)},\, R^{(i)}}$ for $i = 1, 2, \ldots, m$.
   383	\end{proof}

   385	CL functions used in the paper are frequently defined over a ``large'' field

   387	Section~\ref{sec:ldt}).
   388	However, the introspection protocol in Section~\ref{sec:introspection} handles
   389	CL functions defined over $\F_2$.
   390	The following definition and lemma show that CL functions over prime power

     5	/-!
     6	# Distribution infrastructure for the low individual degree test
     7	
     8	Shared distribution definitions: finite-support weighted distributions,
     9	a probability predicate, push-forward distributions, weighted-sum linear maps,
    10	averaging, uniform distribution, and outcome summation.
    11	
    12	Note: this module contributes declarations to the comparator statement closure
    13	of `mainFormal`, which must elaborate in the same environment as the
    14	Mathlib-only `Challenge.lean`.  Keep the full `import Mathlib`; do not narrow
    15	it.  See `docs/comparator.md`, "Environment alignment".
    16	-/
    17	
    18	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    19	
    20	namespace MIPStarRE.LDT
    21	
    22	/-- A finite-support weighted distribution with nonnegative real-valued weights. -/
    23	structure Distribution (α : Type*) where
    24	  support : Finset α := ∅
    25	  weight : α → Error := fun _ => 0
    26	  nonnegative : ∀ a, 0 ≤ weight a := by intro _; positivity
    27	  outsideSupport : ∀ a, a ∉ support → weight a = 0 := by intro _ _; rfl
    28	
    29	namespace Distribution
    30	
    31	/-- The total mass carried by the explicit support of a distribution. -/
    32	def totalWeight {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) : Error :=
    33	  ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a
    34	
    35	/-- A `Distribution` is probabilistic when its total mass is exactly `1`. -/
    36	def IsProbability {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) : Prop :=
    37	  𝒟.totalWeight = 1
    38	
    39	/-- Push a finite-support distribution forward along a map.
    40	
    41	This is the project `Distribution` analogue of `PMF.map`.  The support is the
    42	image of the original finite support, and each new weight is the sum of the
    43	weights in the corresponding fiber. -/
    44	noncomputable def map {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    45	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) : Distribution β where
    46	  support := 𝒟.support.image e
    47	  weight := fun b => ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b), 𝒟.weight a
    48	  nonnegative := fun _ => Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => 𝒟.nonnegative a
    49	  outsideSupport := fun _ hb =>
    50	    Finset.sum_eq_zero fun a ha =>
    51	      (hb (Finset.mem_image.mpr
    52	        ⟨a, (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).1, (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2⟩)).elim
    53	
    54	@[simp]
    55	theorem map_support {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    56	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) :
    57	    (𝒟.map e).support = 𝒟.support.image e := rfl
    58	
    59	@[simp]
    60	theorem map_weight {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    61	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) (b : β) :
    62	    (𝒟.map e).weight b =
    63	      ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b), 𝒟.weight a := rfl
    64	
    65	/-- Push-forward preserves total mass. -/
    66	theorem map_totalWeight {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    67	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) :
    68	    (𝒟.map e).totalWeight = 𝒟.totalWeight := by
    69	  simpa [totalWeight, map] using
    70	    (Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to
    71	      (s := 𝒟.support) (t := 𝒟.support.image e) (g := e)
    72	      (fun a ha => Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩) 𝒟.weight)
    73	
    74	/-- A finite weighted sum over a push-forward distribution is the corresponding
    75	weighted sum of the pulled-back family.  This is the `Distribution` analogue of
    76	the finite-sum form of `PMF.map`. -/
    77	theorem map_sum_smul {α β M : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    78	    [AddCommMonoid M] [Module Error M]
    79	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) (f : β → M) :
    80	    ∑ b ∈ (𝒟.map e).support, (𝒟.map e).weight b • f b =
    81	      ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a • f (e a) := by
    82	  classical
    83	  calc
    84	    ∑ b ∈ 𝒟.support.image e,
    85	        (∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b), 𝒟.weight a) • f b
    86	        = ∑ b ∈ 𝒟.support.image e,
    87	            ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b), 𝒟.weight a • f (e a) := by
    88	          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
    89	          intro b _
    90	          rw [Finset.sum_smul]
    91	          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
    92	          intro a ha
    93	          exact congrArg (fun x => 𝒟.weight a • f x) (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2.symm
    94	    _ = ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a • f (e a) := by
    95	          exact Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to
    96	            (s := 𝒟.support) (t := 𝒟.support.image e) (g := e)
    97	            (fun a ha => Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩)
    98	            (fun a => 𝒟.weight a • f (e a))
    99	
   100	end Distribution
   101	
   102	/-- On a finite ambient type, a summand that vanishes outside a distribution's
   103	explicit support has the same total sum over all ambient values as over that support.
   104	
   105	This is a project-local explicit-support adapter around Mathlib's `Finset.sum_subset`:
   106	Mathlib supplies the finite-sum theorem, while this lemma packages the common shape used
   107	when paper expressions sum over a whole question set but the repository stores a smaller
   108	`Distribution.support`.  It is not intended to replace Mathlib probability theory. -/
   109	theorem Distribution.sum_univ_eq_sum_support {α β : Type*} [Fintype α]
   110	    [AddCommMonoid β] (𝒟 : Distribution α) (f : α → β)
   111	    (hf : ∀ a, a ∉ 𝒟.support → f a = 0) :
   112	    (∑ a : α, f a) = ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, f a := by
   113	  classical
   114	  simpa using
   115	    (Finset.sum_subset (Finset.subset_univ 𝒟.support)
   116	      (fun a _ ha => hf a ha)).symm
   117	
   118	namespace Distribution.IsProbability
   119	
   120	/-- Unpack the equality form of the probability invariant. -/
   121	theorem weight_sum_eq_one {α : Type*}
   122	    {𝒟 : Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) :
   123	    ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a = 1 := by
   124	  simpa [Distribution.IsProbability, Distribution.totalWeight] using h𝒟
   125	
   126	/-- On a finite ambient type, a probabilistic `Distribution` has total weight `1` even
   127	when its weights are summed over the whole ambient type.
   128	
   129	This packages the explicit-support bookkeeping in `Distribution` for downstream Lean
   130	statements that follow the paper's notation `𝔼_{x ∼ 𝒟}` over the question set rather
   131	than over a stored support finset. -/
   132	theorem weight_sum_univ_eq_one {α : Type*} [Fintype α]
   133	    {𝒟 : Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) :
   134	    (∑ a : α, 𝒟.weight a) = 1 := by
   135	  rw [Distribution.sum_univ_eq_sum_support 𝒟 𝒟.weight 𝒟.outsideSupport]
   136	  exact h𝒟.weight_sum_eq_one
   137	
   138	/-- A probability distribution has total weight at most `1`. -/
   139	theorem weight_sum_le_one {α : Type*}
   140	    {𝒟 : Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) :
   141	    ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a ≤ 1 :=
   142	  le_of_eq h𝒟.weight_sum_eq_one
   143	
   144	/-- Push-forward preserves the probability invariant. -/
   145	theorem map {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
   146	    {𝒟 : Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) (e : α → β) :
   147	    (𝒟.map e).IsProbability := by
   148	  simpa [Distribution.IsProbability, Distribution.map_totalWeight] using h𝒟
   149	
   150	end Distribution.IsProbability
   151	
   152	namespace Distribution
   153	
   154	/-- The Mathlib probability mass function associated to a project `Distribution`
   155	whose total mass is one.
   156	
   157	The construction sends each nonnegative real weight to `ℝ≥0∞` by
   158	`ENNReal.ofReal`; the hypotheses of `PMF.ofFinset` are exactly the project
   159	probability invariant and the stored zero-off-support condition. -/
   160	noncomputable def toPMF {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α)
   161	    (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) : PMF α :=
   162	  PMF.ofFinset (fun a => ENNReal.ofReal (𝒟.weight a)) 𝒟.support
   163	    (by
   164	      rw [← ENNReal.ofReal_sum_of_nonneg (fun a _ => 𝒟.nonnegative a),
   165	        h𝒟.weight_sum_eq_one]
   166	      simp)
   167	    (by
   168	      intro a ha
   169	      rw [𝒟.outsideSupport a ha]
   170	      simp)

+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.DistanceTheorems
+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.ErrorFunctions
+
+/-! # Sandwiched measurements and pasting
+
+This module defines the ordered palindromic products used to combine
+measurements and records the two quantitative consistency statements imported
+by the QPBT analysis.
+
+## References
+
+The source results are `lem:ld-sandwich` and `lem:pasting` in
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:398-470`, with paper origin
+`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:465-525`.
+-/
+
+open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
+
+/-- The ordered product
+`G^k_{g_k} ... G^1_{g_1} ... G^k_{g_k}` of `lem:ld-sandwich`.
+
+**Local fix:** The source reverses the outcome indices, which is ill-typed when
+the outcome families differ. This definition uses the pairing corrected in
+`rem:ld-sandwich-indexing`; blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:398-430`, paper
+`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:465-501`.
+The empty product is `1`. -/
+noncomputable def sandwichProduct {k : ℕ} {X ι : Type*}
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {Γ : Fin k → Type*}
+    (G : (i : Fin k) → X → Γ i → Op ι) (x : X)
+    (g : (i : Fin k) → Γ i) : Op ι :=
+  let operators := List.ofFn (fun i : Fin k => G i x (g i))
+  operators.reverse.prod * operators.tail.prod
+
+/-- The two-family sandwiched product
+`(G₂)_{g₂} (G₁)_{g₁} (G₂)_{g₂}` from `eq:pasting-2a`; blueprint
+`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:440-467`, paper
+`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:504-525`. -/
+def pastedMeasurement {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    {G₁ G₂ : Type*} (M₁ : G₁ → Op ι) (M₂ : G₂ → Op ι)
+    (g₁ : G₁) (g₂ : G₂) : Op ι :=
+  M₂ g₂ * M₁ g₁ * M₂ g₂
+
+/-- Evaluating a tuple of codewords at a common point. This is a
+formalization-only auxiliary for `lem:ld-sandwich`, blueprint
+`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:398-423`, paper
+`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:465-495`. -/
+def evalFunctionTuple {k : ℕ} {Y : Type*} {R Γ : Fin k → Type*}
+    (eval : (i : Fin k) → Γ i → Y → R i) (y : Y)
+    (g : (i : Fin k) → Γ i) : (i : Fin k) → R i :=
+  fun i => eval i (g i) y
+
+/-- The palindromic effects form a POVM when each constituent measurement is
+projective. This is the measurement assertion implicit in `lem:ld-sandwich`,
+blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:415-423`, paper
+`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:484-494`. -/
+theorem sandwichProduct_isMeasurement {k : ℕ} {X ι : Type*}
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {Γ : Fin k → Type*}
+    [∀ i, Fintype (Γ i)] (G : (i : Fin k) → X → Measurement (Γ i) ι)
+    (hG : ∀ i x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (G i x)) (x : X) :
+    (∀ g : (i : Fin k) → Γ i,
+      0 ≤ sandwichProduct (fun i x' a => (G i x').effect a) x g) ∧
+      (∑ g : (i : Fin k) → Γ i,
+        sandwichProduct (fun i x' a => (G i x').effect a) x g) = 1 := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- The sandwiched simultaneous-measurement estimate of `lem:ld-sandwich`.
+The universal asymptotic constant is quantified before the distribution,
+measurements, state, and error parameters. Blueprint
+`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:398-423`, paper
+`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:465-501`. -/
+theorem consistencyDefect_sandwich_le :
+    ∃ C₀ : ℝ, 1 ≤ C₀ ∧
+      ∀ {k : ℕ} {X Y ιA ιB : Type*} {R Γ : Fin k → Type*}
+        [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y] [Nonempty Y]
+        [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
+        [∀ i, Fintype (R i)] [∀ i, DecidableEq (R i)]
+        [∀ i, Fintype (Γ i)] [∀ i, DecidableEq (Γ i)]
+        (μ : Distribution X)
+        (eval : (i : Fin k) → Γ i → Y → R i)
+        (G : (i : Fin k) → X → Measurement (Γ i) ιB)
+        (A : X → Measurement ((i : Fin k) → Γ i) ιA)
+        (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) (ε δ : ℝ),
+      μ.IsProbability → ‖ψ‖ = 1 → 0 < ε → 0 ≤ δ →
+      (∀ i x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (G i x)) →
+      (∀ x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (A x)) →
+      (∀ i (g g' : Γ i), g ≠ g' →
+        avgOver (uniformDistribution Y)
+          (fun y => if eval i g y = eval i g' y then 1 else 0) ≤ ε) →
+      (∀ i, consistencyDefect (Distribution.prod μ (uniformDistribution Y))
+        (fun xy a => heteroKron (((A xy.1).postprocess
+          (fun g => eval i (g i) xy.2)).effect a) 1)
+        (fun xy a => heteroKron 1 (((G i xy.1).postprocess
+          (fun g => eval i g xy.2)).effect a)) ψ ≤ δ) →
+      consistencyDefect (Distribution.prod μ (uniformDistribution Y))
+        (fun xy a => heteroKron (((A xy.1).postprocess
+          (evalFunctionTuple eval xy.2)).effect a) 1)
+        (fun xy a => heteroKron 1 (∑ g : (i : Fin k) → Γ i,
+          if evalFunctionTuple eval xy.2 g = a then
+            sandwichProduct (fun i x h => (G i x).effect h) xy.1 g else 0)) ψ ≤
+        C₀ * (k : ℝ) * Real.sqrt (δ + ε) := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- The positive-mass conditional collision bound used by `lem:pasting`.
+This is a formalization-only spelling of the conditional probability in
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:440-467`, with paper origin
+`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:504-525`. -/
+def HasConditionalCollisionBound {X Y₁ Y₂ R₂ Γ₂ : Type*}
+    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype Y₁] [DecidableEq Y₁]
+    [Fintype Y₂] [DecidableEq Y₂] [Fintype R₂] [DecidableEq R₂]
+    [Fintype Γ₂]
+    (D : Distribution ((X × Y₁) × Y₂)) (eval₂ : Γ₂ → Y₂ → R₂)
+    (η : ℝ) : Prop :=
+  ∀ x y₁, 0 < (D.map Prod.fst).weight (x, y₁) →
+    ∀ g g' : Γ₂, g ≠ g' →
+      (∑ y₂ : Y₂, D.weight ((x, y₁), y₂) *
+        if eval₂ g y₂ = eval₂ g' y₂ then 1 else 0) ≤
+        η * (D.map Prod.fst).weight (x, y₁)
+
+/-- The effects obtained by sandwiching one measurement with a projective
+measurement form a POVM. This is the measurement assertion for
+`eq:pasting-2a`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:454-457`, paper
+`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:514-524`. -/
+theorem pastedMeasurement_isMeasurement {Γ₁ Γ₂ ι : Type*}
+    [Fintype Γ₁] [Fintype Γ₂] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    (G₁ : Measurement Γ₁ ι) (G₂ : Measurement Γ₂ ι)
+    (hG₂ : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective G₂) :
+    (∀ g : Γ₁ × Γ₂,
+      0 ≤ pastedMeasurement G₁.effect G₂.effect g.1 g.2) ∧
+      (∑ g : Γ₁ × Γ₂,
+        pastedMeasurement G₁.effect G₂.effect g.1 g.2) = 1 := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- Pasting two consistent measurements yields a product-form polynomial
+error. All operator families in the conclusion are the postprocessed source
+families. This is `lem:pasting`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:440-467`, paper
+`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:504-525`. -/
+theorem exists_pasting_error :
+    ∃ δp : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ, IsPolyErr₂ δp ∧
+      ∀ {X Y₁ Y₂ R₁ R₂ Γ₁ Γ₂ ι : Type*}
+        [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype Y₁] [DecidableEq Y₁]
+        [Fintype Y₂] [DecidableEq Y₂] [Fintype R₁] [DecidableEq R₁]
+        [Fintype R₂] [DecidableEq R₂]
+        [Fintype Γ₁] [DecidableEq Γ₁] [Fintype Γ₂] [DecidableEq Γ₂]
+        [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+        (D : Distribution ((X × Y₁) × Y₂))
+        (eval₁ : Γ₁ → Y₁ → R₁) (eval₂ : Γ₂ → Y₂ → R₂)
+        (G₁ : X → Measurement Γ₁ ι) (G₂ : X → Measurement Γ₂ ι)
+        (A : ((X × Y₁) × Y₂) → Measurement (R₁ × R₂) ι)
+        (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × ι)) (η δ : ℝ),
+        D.IsProbability → ‖ψ‖ = 1 → 0 ≤ η → 0 ≤ δ →
+        (∀ x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (G₂ x)) →
+        (∀ q, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (A q)) →
+        HasConditionalCollisionBound D eval₂ η →
+        consistencyDefect D
+          (fun q a₁ => heteroKron (((A q).postprocess Prod.fst).effect a₁) 1)
+          (fun q a₁ => heteroKron 1 (((G₁ q.1.1).postprocess
+            (fun g => eval₁ g q.1.2)).effect a₁)) ψ ≤ δ →
+        consistencyDefect D
+          (fun q a₂ => heteroKron (((A q).postprocess Prod.snd).effect a₂) 1)
+          (fun q a₂ => heteroKron 1 (((G₂ q.1.1).postprocess
+            (fun g => eval₂ g q.2)).effect a₂)) ψ ≤ δ →
+        consistencyDefect D (fun q a => heteroKron ((A q).effect a) 1)
+          (fun q a => heteroKron 1 ((A q).effect a)) ψ ≤ δ →
+        consistencyDefect D (fun q a => heteroKron ((A q).effect a) 1)
+          (fun q a => heteroKron 1 (∑ g₁ : Γ₁, ∑ g₂ : Γ₂,
+            if (eval₁ g₁ q.1.2, eval₂ g₂ q.2) = a then
+              pastedMeasurement (fun g => (G₁ q.1.1).effect g)
+                (fun g => (G₂ q.1.1).effect g) g₁ g₂ else 0)) ψ ≤ δp η δ := by
+  sorry
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     2	\label{sec:prelim}
     3	
     4	\paragraph{Notation.}
     5	We use $\Sigma$ to denote a finite alphabet.
     6	$\N$ is the set of positive integers.
     7	For $w\in\{0,1\}$, $\overline{w}$ denotes $1-w$.
     8	For $w\in\{\alice,\bob\}$, $\overline{w}=\bob$ if $w=\alice$ and
     9	$\overline{w}=\alice$ otherwise.
    10	(For notational convenience we often implicitly make the identifications
    11	$1\leftrightarrow \alice$ and $2\leftrightarrow \bob$.)
    12	We use $\F$ to denote a finite field.
    13	We write $M_n(\F)$ to denote the set of $n\times n$ matrices over $\F$.
    14	We write $I$ to denote the identity operator on a vector space.
    15	We write $\Tr(\cdot)$ for the matrix trace.
    16	We write $\mH$ to denote a separable Hilbert space.
    17	For a linear operator $T$, $\|T\|$ denotes the operator norm.
    18	
    19	\paragraph{Asymptotics.}
    20	All logarithms are base $2$.
    21	We use the notation $O(\cdot)$, $\poly(\cdot)$, and $\polylog(\cdot)$ in the
    22	following way.
    23	For $f,g:\N\to\R_+$ we write $f(n)=O(g(n))$ (omitting the integer $n$ when it is
    24	clear from context) to mean that there exists a constant $C>0$ such that for all
    25	$n\in\N$, $f(n)\leq C g(n)$.
    26	When we write $f(a_1,\ldots,a_k) = \poly(a_1,\ldots,a_k)$, this indicates that
    27	there exists a universal constant $C > 0$ (which may vary each time the notation
    28	is used in the paper) such that $f(a_1,\ldots,a_k) \leq C( a_1 \cdots a_k)^C$
    29	for all positive $a_1,\ldots,a_k$.
    30	Similarly, when we write $f(a_1,\ldots,a_k) = \polylog(a_1,\ldots,a_k)$, there
    31	exists a universal constant $C$ such that $f(a_1,\ldots,a_k) \leq C\prod_{i =
    32	  1}^k \log^C (1+ a_i)$ for all positive $a_1,\ldots,a_k$.
    33	Finally, we write $\log(a_1,\ldots,a_k)$ as short hand for $\prod_{i = 1}^k \log
    34	(1 + a_i)$.\footnote{The additional $1$ in the argument of the $\log(\cdot)$ is
    35	  to ensure that this quantity is strictly positive.}

    37	\subsection{Turing machines}
    38	\label{sec:tms}
    39	
    40	Turing machines are a model of computation introduced
    41	in~\cite{turing1937computable}, and play a central role in our modeling of verifiers for nonlocal
    42	games. Here we give an overview of certain aspects of Turing machines that are relevant for
    43	this paper. For an in-depth treatment of Turing machines, we refer the reader to the textbooks of 
    44	Papadimitriou~\cite{Pap94} or Sipser~\cite{sipser2012introduction}.

    52	Both constructors carry the assertion that their base is fixed by the
    53	appropriate `lineRepMap`. A value `j : Fin L.m` represents the paper's
    54	one-based coordinate `j + 1`. -/
    55	inductive LineDesc (L : LdParams) where
    56	  | axis (base : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (seed : ScalarQ L)
    57	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex L seed)) base = base)
    58	  | diagonal (base : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (seed : ScalarQ L)
    59	      (direction : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)
    60	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap direction base = base)
    61	      (prefixZero : ∀ j : Fin L.m, j.val < (chiIndex L seed).val → direction j = 0)
    62	  deriving DecidableEq
    63	
    64	/-- The tag of a canonical line description. -/
    65	def LineDesc.kind {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → LineKind
    66	  | .axis _ _ _ => .axis
    67	  | .diagonal _ _ _ _ _ => .diagonal
    68	
    69	/-- The seed retained by a canonical line description. -/
    70	def LineDesc.seed {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → ScalarQ L
    71	  | .axis _ seed _ => seed
    72	  | .diagonal _ seed _ _ _ => seed
    73	
    74	/-- The canonical base stored by a line description. -/
    75	def LineDesc.base {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → Fin L.m → ScalarQ L
    76	  | .axis base _ _ => base
    77	  | .diagonal base _ _ _ _ => base
    78	
    79	/-- The geometric direction represented by a canonical line description.
    80	Diagonal constructors already store the projected data, so this accessor does
    81	not apply a second projection. -/
    82	def LineDesc.direction {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
    83	    Fin L.m → ScalarQ L :=
    84	  match line with
    85	  | .axis _ seed _ => coordinateDirection (chiIndex L seed)
    86	  | .diagonal _ _ direction _ _ => direction
    87	
    88	/-- The canonical base is fixed by the representative map of the line's
    89	geometric direction. -/
    90	theorem LineDesc.base_fixed {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
    91	    lineRepMap line.direction line.base = line.base := by
    92	  cases line with
    93	  | axis base seed baseFixed => exact baseFixed
    94	  | diagonal base seed direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact baseFixed
    95	
    96	/-- Every diagonal description carries the source prefix-zero invariant. -/
    97	theorem LineDesc.diagonal_prefix_zero {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L)
    98	    (hline : line.kind = .diagonal) :
    99	    ∀ j : Fin L.m, j.val < (chiIndex L line.seed).val → line.direction j = 0 := by
   100	  cases line with
   101	  | axis base seed baseFixed => simp [LineDesc.kind] at hline
   102	  | diagonal base seed direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact prefixZero
   103	
   104	/-- The point set represented by a seed-bearing line description. -/
   105	noncomputable def LineDesc.pointSet {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
   106	    Set (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) :=
   107	  linePoints line.base line.direction
   108	
   109	/-- Coefficient-list representation of a univariate polynomial of degree at
   110	most `c` over the scalar field of `L`. -/
   111	abbrev DegPoly (L : LdParams) (c : ℕ) := Fin (c + 1) → ScalarQ L
   112	
   113	/-- Evaluate a bounded coefficient-list polynomial. -/
   114	def degPolyEval {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ}
   115	    (f : DegPoly L c) (t : ScalarQ L) : ScalarQ L :=
   116	  ∑ i : Fin (c + 1), f i * t ^ i.val
   117	
   118	/-- Extend a coefficient list by zero from degree bound `c` to `c'`. -/
   119	def DegPoly.padTo {L : LdParams} {c c' : ℕ} (_h : c ≤ c')
   120	    (f : DegPoly L c) : DegPoly L c' :=
   121	  fun i =>
   122	    if hi : i.val < c + 1 then f ⟨i.val, hi⟩ else 0
   123	
   124	/-- A line polynomial evaluates to `a` at `u` when `u` has a line parameter
   125	and every such parameter gives the same value.  The universal clause handles
   126	the zero-direction presentation without choosing a sentinel parameter. -/
   127	def EvaluatesTo {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L)
   128	    (f : DegPoly L c) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (a : ScalarQ L) : Prop :=
   129	  (∃ t : ScalarQ L, u = line.base + t • line.direction) ∧
   130	    ∀ t : ScalarQ L, u = line.base + t • line.direction → degPolyEval f t = a
   131	
   132	/-- Evaluate a line polynomial at a point, returning `none` precisely when the
   133	point does not determine an evaluation.  The `Option` completion is the
   134	paper's bottom outcome for malformed or nonincident answers. -/
   135	noncomputable def evalOpt {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L)
   136	    (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (f : DegPoly L c) : Option (ScalarQ L) := by
   137	  classical
   138	  exact if h : ∃ a : ScalarQ L, EvaluatesTo line f u a then
   139	    some (Classical.choose h)
   140	  else none
   141	
   142	/-- Convert an axis-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation; paper
   143	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257,276-287`. -/
   144	def aLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L :=
   145	  let direction := coordinateDirection (chiIndex L line.seed)
   146	  let base := lineRepMap direction line.point
   147	  LineDesc.axis base line.seed (lineRepMap_apply_self direction line.point)
   148	
   149	/-- Convert a diagonal-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation; paper
   150	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-287`. -/
   151	def dLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L :=
   152	  let direction := prefixProjection (chiIndex L line.seed) line.direction
   153	  let base := lineRepMap direction line.point
   154	  LineDesc.diagonal base line.seed direction
   155	    (lineRepMap_apply_self direction line.point) (by
   156	      intro j hj
   157	      change prefixProjection (chiIndex L line.seed) line.direction j = 0
   158	      rw [prefixProjection, if_pos hj])
   159	
   160	/-- The axis-line/point component of the low-degree line-point sampler; paper
   161	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257,274-287`. -/
   162	noncomputable def aLinePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   163	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   164	  (clDistribution (ldALineCL L) (ldPointCL L)).map fun sample =>
   165	    (aLineDescOf L sample.1, LdSpace.point sample.2)
   166	
   167	/-- The diagonal-line/point component of the low-degree line-point sampler; paper
   168	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-287`. -/
   169	noncomputable def dLinePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   170	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   171	  (clDistribution (ldDLineCL L) (ldPointCL L)).map fun sample =>
   172	    (dLineDescOf L sample.1, LdSpace.point sample.2)
   173	
   174	/-- The equal mixture of axis and diagonal line-point samples from
   175	`def:line-point-dist`; paper
   176	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`. -/
   177	noncomputable def linePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   178	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   179	  Distribution.mix (1 / 2) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
   180	    (aLinePointDist L) (dLinePointDist L)
   181	
   182	/-- The affine line-point component has total probability one. -/
   183	theorem aLinePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   184	    (aLinePointDist L).IsProbability := by
   185	  sorry
   186	
   187	/-- The diagonal line-point component has total probability one. -/
   188	theorem dLinePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   189	    (dLinePointDist L).IsProbability := by
   190	  sorry
   191	
   192	/-- The line-point mixture has total probability one. -/
   193	theorem linePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   194	    (linePointDist L).IsProbability := by
   195	  exact Distribution.mix_isProbability _ _ _
   196	    (aLinePointDist_isProbability L) (dLinePointDist_isProbability L)
   197	    (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
   198	
   199	end

130	  Let $u,v \in \F_q^m$.
   131	  Then for all $u' \in \line(u,v)$, we have that $\line(u,v) = \line(u',v)$.
   132	\end{proposition}
   133	\begin{proof}
   134		Fix $u' \in \line(u,v)$.
   135	  We have that $u' = u + tv$ for some $t \in \F_q$.
   136	  Let $a \in \line(u,v)$.
   137	  This means that $a = u + sv$ for some $s\in \F_q$.
   138	  We also have that $a = u + (s - t + t)v = u + tv + (s - t)v = u' + (s - t)v$,
   139	  so $\line(u,v) \subseteq \line(u',v)$.
   140	  A similar argument shows that $\line(u',v) \subseteq \line(u,v)$.
   141	\end{proof}
   142	
   143	We now specify a canonical representation of lines $\line = \line(u,v)$ as pairs $(u_0,v)$
   144	where $u_0$ is a \emph{canonical representative} of $\line$ specified as
   145	follows.
   146	Let $L_v^{\lnf}: \F_q^m \to \F_q^m$ denote the canonical linear map with the
   147	one-dimensional kernel basis $\{v\}$ (see \Cref{def:cl-canonical} for a
   148	definition of canonical linear map).
   149	Note that for all $u \in \line$, we have that $L_v^{\lnf}(u)$ is a point in
   150	$\line$.
   151	This is because since the image and kernel of $L_v^{\lnf}$ are complementary
   152	subspaces by definition (see \Cref{def:cl-canonical}), any $u \in \F_q^m$ has a
   153	unique decomposition $u = u_0 + u_1$ where $u_0$ is in the image of $L_v^{\lnf}$
   154	and $u_1 \in \ker(L_v^{\lnf})$, which by definition is the subspace spanned by
   155	$v$.
   156	Thus $u_1 = tv$ for some $t \in \F_q$ and we have that $u_0 = u - tv \in \line$.
   157	In particular, if $u\in \line$ then $u_0 = L_v^{\lnf}(u) \in \line$ as well. 
   158	Furthermore, since $L_v^{\lnf}$ is a projection onto its image by definition, we
   159	have $L_v^{\lnf}(u_0) = u_0$.
   160	
   161	Next, note that for any $u,u' \in \line$, since $u-u' = sv$ for some $s\in \F_q$
   162	it follows that $L_v^\lnf(u) = L_v^\lnf(u')$.
   163	Thus $u_0 = u_0'$ and this shows that $L_v^\lnf$ gives a means to compute a
   164	canonical representative of lines.
   165	
   166	\begin{definition}[Canonical representative of a line]
   167	  \label{def:line-representative}
   168	  Let $\line$ be a line in direction $v$.
   169	  A canonical representative of $\line$ is the point $u_0 \in \F_q^m$ such that
   170	  \[
   171	    u_0 = L_v^\lnf(u)
   172	  \]
   173	  for all $u \in \line$.
   174	\end{definition}

   178	\paragraph{Question distribution.}
   179	We now present the question distribution of the game $\game^\ld$ as a typed CL
   180	distribution (see \Cref{sec:types} for the definition of typed CL functions and
   181	typed CL distributions).
   182	The type set $\type^\ld$ of the game $\game^\ld$ we use is
   183	\[
   184		\type^\ld = \{ \Point, \ALine, \DLine \}\;.
   185	\]
   186	The distribution over question types is uniform over $\type^\ld \times \type^\ld$. 
   187	
   188	We introduce the corresponding typed CL functions $L_\Point$, $L_\ALine$,
   189	$L_\DLine$ where the corresponding CL distributions $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$
   190	and $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$ implement the axis line-versus-point and diagonal
   191	line-versus-point distributions, respectively.
   192	The functions are parametrized by a field size $q$, a dimension $m$, and three
   193	complementary register subspaces $V_\xpt,V_{\coord}, V_{\dir{}}$ of some ambient
   194	space.
   195	The register $V_\xpt$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q^m$) is called the
   196	\emph{point register}, $V_\coord$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q$) is called the
   197	\emph{coordinate register}, and $V_{\dir{}}$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q^m$)
   198	is called the \emph{direction register}, respectively.
   199	We let $V$ denote the direct sum $V_\xpt \oplus V_{\coord} \oplus V_{\dir{}}$.
   200	We identify elements of $V$ as triples $(u,s,v) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q \times
   201	\F_q^m$.
   202	
   203	Define $L_\Point$ to be the $1$-level CL function that projects onto $V_\xpt$: for every $(u,s,v) \in V$,
   204	\begin{equation}
   205	  \label{eq:cl-ptf}
   206		L_\Point(u,s,v) = (u,0,0) \;.
   207	\end{equation}
   208	Define $L_\ALine$ to be the following $2$-level CL function:
   209	\begin{equation}
   210	  \label{eq:cl-alnf}
   211		L_\ALine(u,s,v) = (L^\lnf_{e_i}(u), s, 0)\ \text{for all } (u,s,v) \in V,
   212	\end{equation}
   213	where $L^\lnf$ is the linear function used to compute the canonical
   214	representative of lines (see \Cref{def:line-representative}), and $i = \chi(s)$
   215	where we define $\chi(s)$ to be the unique integer such that
   216	\begin{equation}
   217	\label{eq:chi-func}
   218		s = (\chi(s) - 1) \frac{q}{m} + r
   219	\end{equation}
   220	for some $0 \leq r < q/m$, and we interpret the field element $s \in \F_q$ as an
   221	integer between $0$ and $q - 1$).
   222	The function $L_\ALine$ is the concatenation of the $1$-level CL function that
   223	projects the subspaces $V_{\coord} \oplus V_{\dir{}}$ down to $V_\coord$ (i.e.
   224	zeroes out the entire $V_{\dir{}}$ register), and the family of $1$-level CL
   225	functions $\{L^\lnf_{e_i} \}$ acting on $V_\xpt$, indexed by $i \in
   226	\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$.
   227	(See \Cref{lem:cl-concat} for definition of CL function concatenation.)
   228	Thus $L_\ALine$ is a $2$-level CL function.
   229	
   230	Define $L_\DLine$ to be the following $3$-level CL function: for all $(u,s,v) \in
   231	V$,
   232	\begin{equation}
   233	\label{eq:cl-dlnf}
   234		L_\DLine(u,s,v) = (L^\lnf_{\pi_{i-1}(v)}(u),s,\pi_{i-1}(v))
   235	\end{equation}
   236	where $i = \chi(s)$.
   237	The function $L_\DLine$ is the concatenation of the following CL functions (again, see \Cref{lem:cl-concat} for definition of CL function concatenation): (i) the identity function on $V_{\coord}$ (which is a $1$-level CL function); (ii) for every $i \in \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ the $1$-level CL function on $V_{\dir{}}$ that maps $v \mapsto \pi_{i-1}(v)$ (i.e.~it zeroes out the first $i-1$ coordinates of $v$), and (iii) for every pair $(s,v') \in V_\coord \oplus V_{\dir{}}$, the $1$-level CL function $L^\lnf_{v'}$ acting on $V_\xpt$. Thus $L_\DLine$ is a $3$-level CL function.

   240	The following two lemmas establish that the CL functions
   241	$L_\Point,L_\ALine,L_\DLine$ give rise to the axis-parallel line-versus-point and
   242	diagonal line-versus-point distributions.
   243	\begin{lemma}
   244		\label{lem:alnf}
   245		Consider the pair $(\line, u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the
   246	  tuple $((u_0,s,0),(u,0,0))$ from the CL distribution $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$,
   247	  and let $\line = \line(u_0,e_i)$ where $i = \chi(s)$.
   248	  Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\F_q^m$ and $\line$ is a line that
   249	  goes through $u$ and is parallel to a uniformly random axis $i \in
   250	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$.
   251	\end{lemma}
   252	\begin{proof}
   253		Since $s$ is uniformly random in $\F_q$ and $m$ divides $q$ by assumption, we
   254	  have that $i$ is uniformly random between $\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ and therefore
   255	  $(u_0,s)$ specifies a uniformly random axis-parallel line $\line(u_0,e_i)$.
   256	  Since $u_0 = L^{\lnf}_{e_i}(u)$, we have that $u \in \line(u_0,e_i)$.
   257	\end{proof}

   261	\begin{lemma}
   262		\label{lem:dlnf}
   263		Consider the pair $(\line,u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the
   264	  tuple $((u_0,s,v),(u,0,0))$ from the CL distribution $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$,
   265	  and let $\line = \line(u_0,v)$ where $i = \chi(s)$.
   266	  Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\F_q^m$ and $\line$ is a random
   267	  diagonal line that goes through $u$ and shares the first $i-1$ coordinates
   268	  with $u$, for uniformly random $i$.
   269	\end{lemma}
   270	\begin{proof}
   271		The proof of this follows identically to \Cref{lem:alnf}.
   272	\end{proof}

   320	\paragraph{Decision procedure} The decision procedure $\decider^\ld$ for the
   321	game $\game^\ld$ is presented in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider}.
   322	The table at the top specifies a parsing scheme for the questions and answers,
   323	depending on the type of question.
   324	For example, when a player receives a question with type $\Point$, the question
   325	content $x$, a bit string of length $m \log q$, should be interpreted by the
   326	decision procedure and the players as an element of the vector space $\F_q^m$,
   327	as indicated in Section~\ref{sec:ff-representations}.
   328	Similarly the answer to a question with type $\Point$ is expected to be a bit
   329	string of length $\ldc \log q$, and is interpreted as an element of $\F_q^\ldc$.
   330	For questions with type $\ALine$, the question content is a $(m \log q + \log
   331	q)$-bit string, which is parsed as a pair $(u_0, s) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q$,
   332	which in turn can be interpreted as a specification for an axis-parallel line
   333	$\line(u_0,e_i)$ in $\F_q^m$ where $i = \chi(s)$, as described in
   334	\Cref{lem:alnf}.
   335	The answer is interpreted as the description of $\ldc$ degree-$d$ univariate
   336	polynomials defined on the line $\line(u_0,e_i)$, each polynomial given by a
   337	list of $d+1$ coefficients.
   338	For questions with type $\DLine$, the question content is a $(2m \log q + \log
   339	q)$-bit string, which is parsed as a triple $(u_0, s, v) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q
   340	\times \F_q^m$ that specifies a diagonal line $\line(u_0,v')$ where $v' =
   341	\pi_{i-1}(v)$ as described in \Cref{lem:dlnf}.
   342	The answer is interpreted as the description of $\ldc$ degree-$md$ univariate
   343	polynomials defined on the line $\line(u_0,v')$.
   344	If the answers returned by the players do not fit this format the decision
   345	procedure rejects.

   394	We define a special class of measurements that are relevant to the soundness
   395	properties of the low-degree test.
   396	
   397	\begin{definition}[Low-degree polynomial measurements]
   398	  \label{def:ld-meas}
   399	  Define $\polymeas{m}{d}{q}$ to be the set of POVM measurements whose outcomes
   400	  correspond to (individual) degree-$d$ polynomials of $m$ variables over
   401	  $\F_q$.
   402	  More generally, for an integer $\ldc$ and tuples $m=(m_1, m_2, \ldots,
   403	  m_\ldc)$, $d=(d_1, d_2, \ldots, d_\ldc)$ and $q=(q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_\ldc)$,
   404	  we let $\simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}$ be the set of measurements $G =
   405	  \{G_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots\,,\, g_\ldc}\}$ such that for $i\in\{1, 2, \ldots,
   406	  \ldc\}$, $g_i$ is a polynomial $g_i:\F_{q_i}^{m_i} \rightarrow
   407	  \F_{q_i}$ with individual degree $d_i$ (see \Cref{sec:ld-encoding} for a definition of individual degree). 
   408	\end{definition}
   409	
   410	Quantum soundness of a version of the classical low-degree test for polynomials of low \emph{total} degree was claimed
   411	in~\cite{natarajan2018low}, building on an analysis of a three-prover version of the test in~\cite{vidick2016three}. Unfortunately there is a gap in the soundness analysis of this test. For our construction we use the low individual degree test, whose quantum soundness is shown in~\cite{ML20} and generalized in~\cite{ji2021quantum}. We state the result in the form that is most directly useful for us, and show how the stated result follows from~\cite{ji2021quantum}.
   412	
   413	\begin{theorem}[Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low-degree test]
   414	  \label{lem:ld-soundness}
   415	  There exists a function $\delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc) = a (dm \ldc)^a (\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for universal constants $a\geq 1$ and $0<b\leq 1$ 
   416	such that the following
   417	  holds.
   418	  For all $\eps > 0$ and parameter tuple $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$, for all

   445	and $m$ divides $q$. Let $\Sigma=\F_q$. Let $\code \subseteq \Sigma^q$ be the Reed-Solomon code with degree $d$. Explicitly, $\code$ is the set of all $(p(x_1),\ldots,p(x_n))$ where $p:\F_q\to\F_q$ is a univariate polynomial of degree at most $d$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ are an enumeration of $\F_q$.   1492	\subsubsection{Canonical parameters and complexity of the Pauli basis test}
  1493	\label{sec:qld-complexity}
  1494	
  1495	We specify a canonical setting of the parameter tuple $\qldparams$ as a function
  1496	of an integer $R$.
  1497	We call this canonical setting $\introparams$ because we use these in the
  1498	``introspection'' section (\Cref{sec:introspection}).
  1499	We then give bounds on the complexity of computing the decision procedure and CL
  1500	functions of the Pauli basis test corresponding to the parameter tuple
  1501	$\qldparams$, as a function of $R$.
  1502	
  1503	\begin{definition}[Canonical parameters of the Pauli basis test]
  1504	  \label{def:introparams}
  1505	  Let $a,b$ be the universal constants specified in Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}.
  1506	  Let $c$ denote the smallest even integer that is at least $(b + a)/b$.
  1507	  For all integers $R \geq 4$, define the tuple $\introparams(R) = (q,m,d)$
  1508	  where
  1509	  \begin{itemize}
  1510	  	\item $q = 2^k$ for $k = c \lceil  \log \log R  \rceil + 1$.
  1511		\item $m = 2^j$ where $2^j \leq c \lceil \log R \rceil + 1 < 2^{j+1}$. 
  1512		\item $d = 1$. 
  1513	  \end{itemize}
  1514	\end{definition}
  1515	
  1516	Intuitively, this choice of parameters is such that the Pauli basis test
  1517	certifies the presence of an $M=2^m$-qudit EPR state (of local dimension $q$), or
  1518	equivalently an $M\log q$-qubit EPR state.
  1519	
  1520	\begin{lemma}
  1521	  \label{lem:delta-bound}
  1522	 For all integers $R \geq 4$, the parameter tuple $\introparams(R) = (q,m,d)$ is
  1523	  admissible (see Definition~\ref{def:admissible}), satisfies $2^m \geq R$, and furthermore there exist
  1524	  universal constants $a'\geq 1$ and $0 < b' \leq 1$ such that the function
  1525	  $\delta_\qld(\eps, m, d, q)$ from Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli} is at most
  1526	   \[
  1527	   	a' ( \log(R)^{a'} \cdot \eps^{b'} + \log(R)^{-b'}) \;.
  1528		\]
  1529	\end{lemma}
  1530	
  1531	\begin{proof}
  1532	  We verify the admissibility of $\introparams(R)$ first: the field size $q =
  1533	  2^k$ is admissible because $k$ is odd. We have $m | q$ because for all $R \geq 4$ we have  
  1534	  \[
  1535	  	2^j \leq 2 c \lceil \log R \rceil \leq 2 \log^c R \leq 2^k~.
  1536	  \]
  1537		Next, we show that $R \leq 2^m$. Since $m = 2^j \geq (c/2) \log R$, we have that
  1538		\[
  1539			2^m \geq R^{c/2} \geq R
  1540		\]
  1541		where we used that $c \geq 2$. 
  1542	
  1543	Finally, we show the desired bound on the error function $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q)$. First, observe that $2^{-bmd} \leq q^{-b}$ because $k \leq m$.
  1544	  Note that for $R \geq 2$, we have $m \leq 2c \log R$, and furthermore $q =
  1545	  2^k \geq \log^c R$.
  1546	Then, we get
  1547	\begin{align*}
  1548	  	\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q)
  1549	    & = a (md)^a (\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd}) \tag{by Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}}  \\
  1550	    & \leq a (md)^a (\eps^b + 2q^{-b}) \tag{because  $2^{-bmd} \leq q^{-b}$}  \\
  1551	    & = a (m)^a (\eps^b + 2q^{-b}) \tag{because  $d=1$}  \\
  1552	    & \leq a (2c)^a \log^{a} (R) ( \eps^{b} + 2q^{-b}) \tag{because  $m \leq 2c \log R$}\\
  1553	    & \leq a (2c)^a \log^{a} (R) ( \eps^{b} + 2(\log R)^{-cb}) \tag{because  $q \geq \log^c R$}\\
  1554	    & \leq 2a (2c)^a \log^{a} (R) ( \eps^{b} + (\log R)^{-cb}) \\
  1555	    & = 2a (2c)^a ( (\log R)^{a}\eps^{b} + (\log R)^{a-cb}) \\
  1556	    & \leq 2a(2c)^{a} \left ( (\log R)^{a} \eps^{b}
  1557	      + (\log R)^{-b} \right) \tag{because  $cb - a \geq b \geq 0$}\\
  1558	    & \leq a' ( (\log R)^{a'} \eps^{b} + (\log R)^{-b}),
  1559	  \end{align*}
  1560	  where $a'$ is defined as the quantity $2a(2c)^a$.
  1561	This completes the proof of the lemma.
  1562	\end{proof}
  1563	
  1564	\begin{lemma}
  1565		\label{lem:introparams-complexity}
  1566		Fix an integer $R \geq 4$, let $\introparams(R) = (q,m,d)$.
  1567		The integers $(q,m,d) = \introparams(R)$ can be computed in time $\polylog
  1568	  R$ when given the binary representation of $R$ as input.
  1569	\end{lemma}

   171	/-!
   172	# Qubit form of Pauli basis test soundness
   173	
   174	The fixed self-dual normal basis converts the qudit EPR register and generalized
   175	Pauli projectors into qubit coordinates. The conversion uses only the basis
   176	stored in the canonical `FixedFieldModel`.
   177	
   178	## References
   179	
   180	The conversion is `lem:pauli-binary` in
   181	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:675-708`, from
   182	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1163-1208`. The resulting
   183	`cor:pauli-binary` is in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:409-435`,
   184	from `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1450-1501`.
   185	-/
   186	
   187	open scoped BigOperators Matrix
   188	
   189	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
   190	
   191	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
   192	
   193	noncomputable section
   194	
   195	/-- The bit register obtained by expanding every Pauli-register field element
   196	in the basis stored by `P.model`. -/
   197	abbrev QubitRegister (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   198	  Cube P.m × Fin P.model.basisDim → ZMod 2
   199	
   200	/-- The ideal auxiliary state tensored with the qubit EPR register, in the
   201	local-player ordering used by `cor:pauli-binary`. -/
   202	noncomputable def idealQubitState (P : AdmissibleParams)
   203	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   204	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   205	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')) :
   206	    EuclideanSpace ℂ
   207	      ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
   208	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv
   209	      ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) ℂ).symm
   210	    (fun p =>
   211	      (EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA' × ιB') ℂ aux (p.1.1, p.2.1)) *
   212	        (EuclideanSpace.equiv (QubitRegister P × QubitRegister P) ℂ
   213	          (eprState (QubitRegister P)) (p.1.2, p.2.2)))
   214	
   215	/-- The local isometries, auxiliary spaces, and unit auxiliary state in
   216	`cor:pauli-binary`; this structure introduces no hypothesis beyond the paper
   217	theorem. -/
   218	structure QubitSoundnessWitness (P : AdmissibleParams)
   219	    (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)) where
   220	  ιA' : Type
   221	  ιB' : Type
   222	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA']
   223	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB']
   224	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA']
   225	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB']
   226	  φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   227	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × QubitRegister P)
   228	  φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   229	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × QubitRegister P)
   230	  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')
   231	  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1
   232	
   233	attribute [instance] QubitSoundnessWitness.ιAFintype
   234	  QubitSoundnessWitness.ιBFintype QubitSoundnessWitness.ιADecidableEq
   235	  QubitSoundnessWitness.ιBDecidableEq
   236	
   237	/-- Alice's ideal qubit projector placed on the joint target space. -/
   238	noncomputable def qubitProjOnA'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
   239	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   240	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
   241	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
   242	    Op ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
   243	  fun p q =>
   244	    if p.1.1 = q.1.1 ∧ p.2 = q.2 then
   245	      qubitPauliProj W (kappaVec P.model u) p.1.2 q.1.2
   246	    else 0
   247	
   248	/-- Bob's ideal qubit projector placed on the joint target space. -/
   249	noncomputable def qubitProjOnB'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
   250	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   251	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
   252	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
   253	    Op ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
   254	  fun p q =>
   255	    if p.1 = q.1 ∧ p.2.1 = q.2.1 then
   256	      qubitPauliProj W (kappaVec P.model u) p.2.2 q.2.2
   257	    else 0
   258	
   259	/-- Lift a conjugated Alice effect to the full qubit target space. -/
   260	noncomputable def liftedQubitAEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   261	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   262	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   263	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   264	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × QubitRegister P))
   265	    (M : Op S.ιA) :
   266	    Op ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
   267	  heteroKron (conjIsometry φA M) 1
   268	
   269	/-- Lift a conjugated Bob effect to the full qubit target space. -/
   270	noncomputable def liftedQubitBEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   271	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   272	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   273	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   274	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × QubitRegister P))
   275	    (M : Op S.ιB) :
   276	    Op ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
   277	  heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB M)
   278	
   279	/-- Alice's qubit-projector family distance in `cor:pauli-binary`. -/
   280	noncomputable def qubitOperatorDistanceA
   281	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   282	    (w : QubitSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   283	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   284	    ‖applyOperatorToState
   285	      (liftedQubitAEffect S w.φA
   286	          ((S.A (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   287	        qubitProjOnA'' P W u)
   288	      (idealQubitState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   289	
   290	/-- Bob's qubit-projector family distance in `cor:pauli-binary`. -/
   291	noncomputable def qubitOperatorDistanceB
   292	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   293	    (w : QubitSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   294	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   295	    ‖applyOperatorToState
   296	      (liftedQubitBEffect S w.φB
   297	          ((S.B (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   298	        qubitProjOnB'' P W u)
   299	      (idealQubitState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   300	
   301	/-- `cor:pauli-binary`: soundness of the Pauli basis test in qubit
   302	coordinates. Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:409-435`, paper
   303	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1450-1501`.
   304	
   305	The theorem retains the source-compatible nonnegative error boundary and uses
   306	only `P.model` and its stored basis dimension. -/
   307	theorem pauli_soundness_qubit :
   308	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b < 1 ∧
   309	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε →
   310	        ∀ S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P), 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
   311	          ∃ w : QubitSoundnessWitness P S,
   312	            ‖isometryTensor w.φA w.φB S.ψ - idealQubitState P w.aux‖ ≤
   313	                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ∧
   314	            (∀ W : PauliKind,
   315	              qubitOperatorDistanceA P S w W ≤
   316	                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) ∧
   317	            ∀ W : PauliKind,
   318	              qubitOperatorDistanceB P S w W ≤
   319	                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q := by
   320	  sorry
   321	
   322	end
   323	
   324	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     4	# Finite-dimensional state transformations
     5	
     6	This file defines the tensor and reindexing operations used to transport states

    14	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

    17	
    18	/-- Conjugation by the local isometries in `thm:ms-rigidity` and
    19	`lem:pauli-binary`; blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403` and
    20	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:675-708`, paper `08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`. -/
    21	noncomputable def conjIsometry {ι ι' : Type*}
    22	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
    23	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι')
    24	    (M : Op ι) : Op ι' :=
    25	  let U : Matrix ι' ι ℂ := Matrix.toEuclideanLin.symm φ.toLinearMap
    26	  U * M * Uᴴ
    27	
    28	/-- Coordinate transport used by `def:strategy-distance`, blueprint
    29	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:212-219`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:273-285`. -/
    30	noncomputable def reindexState {ι ι' : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    31	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι'] (e : ι ≃ ι')
    32	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι' :=
    33	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι' ℂ).symm
    34	    (fun j => (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ ψ) (e.symm j))
    35	
    36	/-- Apply the two independent local isometries of `thm:ms-rigidity`; blueprint
    37	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper
    38	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`. -/
    39	noncomputable def isometryTensor
    40	    {ιA ιB κA κB : Type*}
    41	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    42	    [Fintype κA] [DecidableEq κA] [Fintype κB] [DecidableEq κB]
    43	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κA)
    44	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κB)
    45	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
    46	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (κA × κB) :=
    47	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv (κA × κB) ℂ).symm
    48	    (fun p =>
    49	      ∑ i : ιA, ∑ j : ιB,
    50	        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv κA ℂ)
    51	            (φA ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ιA ℂ).symm (Pi.single i 1))) p.1) *
    52	          ((EuclideanSpace.equiv κB ℂ)
    53	            (φB ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ιB ℂ).symm (Pi.single j 1))) p.2) *
    54	          ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA × ιB) ℂ) ψ (i, j)))
    55	
    56	/-- Coordinate tensor used in the ideal state of `thm:ms-rigidity`; blueprint
    57	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper
    58	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`. -/
    59	noncomputable def vecTensor {ι κ : Type*}
    60	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ]
    61	    (u : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ κ) :
    62	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × κ) :=
    63	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv (ι × κ) ℂ).symm
    64	    (fun p => (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ u) p.1 * (EuclideanSpace.equiv κ ℂ v) p.2)
    65	
    66	/-- Operator transport used by `def:strategy-distance`, blueprint
    67	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:212-219`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:273-285`. -/
    68	def reindexOp {ι ι' : Type*} (e : ι ≃ ι') (M : Op ι') : Op ι :=
    69	  (Matrix.reindex e.symm e.symm) M
    70	
    71	/-- Four-factor tensor shuffle used by `thm:ms-rigidity`; blueprint
    72	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper
    73	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`. -/
    74	def prodShuffle {α β γ δ : Type*} :
    75	    (α × β) × (γ × δ) ≃ (α × γ) × (β × δ) where
    76	  toFun p := ((p.1.1, p.2.1), (p.1.2, p.2.2))
    77	  invFun p := ((p.1.1, p.2.1), (p.1.2, p.2.2))
    78	  left_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    79	  right_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    80

   394	We define a special class of measurements that are relevant to the soundness
   395	properties of the low-degree test.
   396	
   397	\begin{definition}[Low-degree polynomial measurements]
   398	  \label{def:ld-meas}
   399	  Define $\polymeas{m}{d}{q}$ to be the set of POVM measurements whose outcomes
   400	  correspond to (individual) degree-$d$ polynomials of $m$ variables over
   401	  $\F_q$.
   402	  More generally, for an integer $\ldc$ and tuples $m=(m_1, m_2, \ldots,
   403	  m_\ldc)$, $d=(d_1, d_2, \ldots, d_\ldc)$ and $q=(q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_\ldc)$,
   404	  we let $\simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}$ be the set of measurements $G =
   405	  \{G_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots\,,\, g_\ldc}\}$ such that for $i\in\{1, 2, \ldots,
   406	  \ldc\}$, $g_i$ is a polynomial $g_i:\F_{q_i}^{m_i} \rightarrow
   407	  \F_{q_i}$ with individual degree $d_i$ (see \Cref{sec:ld-encoding} for a definition of individual degree). 
   408	\end{definition}
   409	
   410	Quantum soundness of a version of the classical low-degree test for polynomials of low \emph{total} degree was claimed
   411	in~\cite{natarajan2018low}, building on an analysis of a three-prover version of the test in~\cite{vidick2016three}. Unfortunately there is a gap in the soundness analysis of this test. For our construction we use the low individual degree test, whose quantum soundness is shown in~\cite{ML20} and generalized in~\cite{ji2021quantum}. We state the result in the form that is most directly useful for us, and show how the stated result follows from~\cite{ji2021quantum}.
   412	
   413	\begin{theorem}[Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low-degree test]
   414	  \label{lem:ld-soundness}
   415	  There exists a function $\delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc) = a (dm \ldc)^a (\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for universal constants $a\geq 1$ and $0<b\leq 1$ 
   416	such that the following
   417	  holds.
   418	  For all $\eps > 0$ and parameter tuple $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$, for all
   419	  projective strategies $(\psi,A,B)$ that succeed with probability at least
   420	  $1-\eps$ in the game $\game^\ld_\ldparams$, there exists measurements
   421	  \[G^w \in \simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}\] on $\mH_w$, for
   422	  $w\in\{\alice,\bob\}$, such that
   423	  \begin{equation*}
   424	    \begin{split}
   425	      A^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}
   426	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   427	      G^\bob_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}\;,\\
   428	      G^\alice_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}
   429	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   430				 B^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}\;,\\
   431	      G^\alice_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}
   432	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   433	      G^\bob_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}\;,
   434	    \end{split}
   435	  \end{equation*}
   436	  where $\delta_{\ld} = \delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc)$, 
   437	  and all three statements are with respect to the state $\ket{\psi}$.
   438	In addition, the first two approximations hold under the uniform distribution over $u\in \F_q^m$,
   439		whereas there is no question distribution associated with the third approximation.
   440	\end{theorem}
   441	
   442	\begin{proof}
   443	Let $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$
   444	where $m, d, \ldc \in \N$ are integers, $q \in \N$ is an admissible field size,
   445	and $m$ divides $q$. Let $\Sigma=\F_q$. Let $\code \subseteq \Sigma^q$ be the Reed-Solomon code with degree $d$. Explicitly, $\code$ is the set of all $(p(x_1),\ldots,p(x_n))$ where $p:\F_q\to\F_q$ is a univariate polynomial of degree at most $d$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ are an enumeration of $\F_q$. Then in the (standard) notation from~\cite{ji2021quantum} $\code$ is a linear $[q,d+1,n-d+1]_\Sigma$ code.

190	/-- The question alphabet for the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
   191	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
   192	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   193	-/
   194	abbrev LdQuestion (P : LdParams) := LdType × LdSpace P
   195	
   196	/-- The typed CL question distribution.  This is the inlined construction in
   197	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
   198	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   199	-/
   200	noncomputable def ldQuestionDistribution (P : LdParams) :
   201	    Distribution (LdQuestion P × LdQuestion P) :=
   202	  Distribution.map
   203	    (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P))
   204	    (fun s =>
   205	      ((s.1.1, ldCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, ldCL P s.1.2 s.2)))
   206	
   207	/-- The coefficient-tuple answer alphabet of the low-degree game.  Polynomial
   208	answers are representatives with exactly the coefficient lengths printed in
   209	the paper, as required by `def:ld-win-predicate` (blueprint
   210	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`; paper
   211	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   212	-/
   213	inductive LdAnswer (P : LdParams) where
   214	  | pointVals (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P)
   215	  | alinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   216	  | dlinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   217	  deriving DecidableEq
   218	
   219	/-- A finite sum code used only to provide the answer alphabet's `Fintype`
   220	instance; the public constructors are those of `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   221	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   222	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   223	-/
   224	abbrev LdAnswerCode (P : LdParams) :=
   225	  (Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   226	    ((Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   227	      (Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P))
   228	
   229	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `LdAnswer` (Lean-only
   230	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   231	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   232	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   233	-/
   234	noncomputable def ldAnswerEquiv (P : LdParams) :
   235	    LdAnswer P ≃ LdAnswerCode P where
   236	  toFun
   237	    | .pointVals a => .inl a
   238	    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
   239	    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
   240	  invFun
   241	    | .inl a => .pointVals a
   242	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
   243	    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
   244	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
   245	  right_inv := by
   246	    intro x
   247	    cases x with
   248	    | inl a => rfl
   249	    | inr x =>
   250	        cases x with
   251	        | inl a => rfl
   252	        | inr a => rfl
   253	
   254	instance (P : LdParams) : Inhabited (LdAnswer P) :=
   255	  ⟨.pointVals (fun _ => 0)⟩
   256	
   257	noncomputable instance (P : LdParams) : Fintype (LdAnswer P) :=
   258	  Fintype.ofEquiv (LdAnswerCode P) (ldAnswerEquiv P).symm
   259	
   260	/-- Evaluation of a coefficient tuple at a field element.  This is the
   261	representative convention used by the line answers in `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   262	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   263	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   264	-/
   265	def evalCoefficient {K : Type*} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ}
   266	    (c : Fin n → K) (t : K) : K :=
   267	  ∑ i : Fin n, c i * t ^ i.val
   268	
   269	/-- Check that an answer has the constructor prescribed by its question type;
   270	Lean encoding of the rejection clause in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   271	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   272	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   273	-/
   274	def validLdAnswer {P : LdParams} (t : LdType) (a : LdAnswer P) : Bool :=
   275	  match t, a with
   276	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   277	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   278	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   279	  | _, _ => false
   280	
   281	/-- The axis-parallel line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   282	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   283	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   284	-/
   285	def alinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   286	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   287	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   288	  -- Universal quantification follows the zero-direction convention in
   289	  -- `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.
   290	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   291	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection (chiIndex P line.seed) →
   292	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   293	
   294	/-- The diagonal line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   295	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   296	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   297	-/
   298	def dlinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   299	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   300	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   301	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   302	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   303	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   304	
   305	/-- The low-degree consistency predicate, rejecting answers of the wrong
   306	constructor shape.  This is `def:ld-win-predicate` in
   307	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   308	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   309	-/
   310	noncomputable def ldWinPredicate (P : LdParams) :
   311	    LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=
   312	  open Classical in
   313	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   314	      if validLdAnswer tA a && validLdAnswer tB b then
   315	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   316	        | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   317	        | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   318	            decide (alinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   319	        | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   320	            decide (alinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   321	        | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   322	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   323	        | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   324	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   325	        | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   326	        | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   327	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   328	      else false
   329	
   330	/-- The low-degree game packaged as a `Game`.  This is `def:ld-game` in
   331	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, paper origin
   332	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   333	-/
   334	noncomputable def ldGame (P : LdParams) : Game where
   335	  QuestionA := LdQuestion P
   336	  QuestionB := LdQuestion P
   337	  AnswerA := LdAnswer P
   338	  AnswerB := LdAnswer P
   339	  μ := ldQuestionDistribution P
   340	  μ_prob := by sorry
   341	  decide := ldWinPredicate P
   342	
   343	end
   344	
   345	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    52	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
