    60	structure AreCloseStrategies (G : Game) (S S' : Strategy G) (δ : ℝ) : Prop where
    61	  /-- Explicit equality of Alice's local spaces. -/
    62	  hA : S.ιA = S'.ιA
    63	  /-- Explicit equality of Bob's local spaces. -/
    64	  hB : S.ιB = S'.ιB
    65	  state : stateDistSq S.ψ (reindexState
    66	      (Equiv.prodCongr (Equiv.cast hA).symm (Equiv.cast hB).symm) S'.ψ) ≤ δ
    67	  alice : opFamilyDistSq (G.μ.map Prod.fst)
    68	      (fun x a => heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) 1)
    69	      (fun x a => heteroKron (reindexOp (Equiv.cast hA) ((S'.A x).effect a)) 1)
    70	      S.ψ ≤ δ
    71	  bob : opFamilyDistSq (G.μ.map Prod.snd)
    72	      (fun y b => heteroKron 1 ((S.B y).effect b))
    73	      (fun y b => heteroKron 1 (reindexOp (Equiv.cast hB) ((S'.B y).effect b)))
    74	      S.ψ ≤ δ

    57	\begin{definition}[Typed conditionally linear functions]
    58	  Let $\type$ be a finite set and $V$ be $\F^n$ for some integer $n \geq 0$.
    59	  A \emph{$\type$-typed family of $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions}
    60	  (implicitly, \emph{on $V$}) is a collection $\{L_\tvar\}_{\tvar \in \type}$
    61	  such that, for each $\tvar \in \type$, $L_\tvar$ is an $\ell$-level
    62	  conditionally linear function on~$V$.
    63	\end{definition}
    64	
    65	\begin{definition}[Graph distribution]
    66	  \label{def:graph-distribution}
    67	  Let $G = (U, E)$ be an undirected graph with vertex set $U$ and edge set~$E$.
    68	  Edges in~$E$ are written as multisets $\{u, v\}$ of two vertices; the case $u
    69	  = v$ represents a self-loop.
    70	  Suppose there are $m$ edges, $k$ of which are self-loops.
    71	  Then the \emph{graph distribution $\mu_G$ of~$G$} is the distribution over
    72	  $U\times U$ such that for every $(u, v)\in U\times U$,
    73	  \begin{equation*}
    74	    \mu_G(u, v) =
    75	    \begin{cases}
    76	      1/(2m-k) & \text{if $\{u, v\} \in E$},\\
    77	      0 & \text{otherwise}.
    78	    \end{cases}
    79	  \end{equation*}
    80	  This is identical to the uniform distribution over pairs $(u, v)\in U\times U$
    81	  such that $\{u, v\} \in E$.
    82	\end{definition}

   240	The following two lemmas establish that the CL functions
   241	$L_\Point,L_\ALine,L_\DLine$ give rise to the axis-parallel line-versus-point and
   242	diagonal line-versus-point distributions.
   243	\begin{lemma}
   244		\label{lem:alnf}
   245		Consider the pair $(\line, u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the
   246	  tuple $((u_0,s,0),(u,0,0))$ from the CL distribution $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$,
   247	  and let $\line = \line(u_0,e_i)$ where $i = \chi(s)$.
   248	  Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\F_q^m$ and $\line$ is a line that
   249	  goes through $u$ and is parallel to a uniformly random axis $i \in
   250	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$.
   251	\end{lemma}
   252	\begin{proof}
   253		Since $s$ is uniformly random in $\F_q$ and $m$ divides $q$ by assumption, we
   254	  have that $i$ is uniformly random between $\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ and therefore
   255	  $(u_0,s)$ specifies a uniformly random axis-parallel line $\line(u_0,e_i)$.
   256	  Since $u_0 = L^{\lnf}_{e_i}(u)$, we have that $u \in \line(u_0,e_i)$.
   257	\end{proof}

   266	  Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\F_q^m$ and $\line$ is a random

   276	\begin{definition}[Line-point distributions]
   277	        \label{def:line-point-dist}
   278	 The \emph{axis line-point distribution} $D_{\ALine}$ is the
   279	 distribution $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$ over pairs $(\ell=(u_0,e_i),u)$

   281	   line-point distribution} $D_{\DLine}$ is the distribution
   282	 $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$  over $(\ell=(u_0,s,v),u)$. The
   283	 \emph{line-point distribution} $D_{\Line}$ is the equal mixture of the axis-parallel line-point distribution and the diagonal line-point distribution.

   285	 with probability $\tfrac{1}{2}$, output a sample from $D_{\ALine}$,
   286	 and with probability $\tfrac{1}{2}$, output a sample from $D_{\DLine}$.

   145	  \label{def:consistent-measurement}

    61	gives $\tau^W(a)^p=I$.  Applying this equality to a nonzero eigenvector gives
    62	$(\lambda^p-1)v=0$, hence $\lambda^p=1$.  Finally, when
    63	$v\notin V^\perp$, the map $u\mapsto\chi(u\cdot v)$ is a nontrivial character
    64	of the finite additive group $V$, so its average vanishes.

    34	\section{Key theorem forms}
    35	
    36	Let $a\geq 1$ and $0<b<1$ be the universal constants in the soundness
    37	function
    38	\[
    39	  \delta_{\mathrm{qld}}(\eps,m,d,q)
    40	    = a(md)^a\bigl(\eps^b+q^{-b}+2^{-bmd}\bigr).
    41	\]
    42	For the canonical parameters, $d=1$, $q=2^k$, and
    43	$m\geq (c/2)\log R\geq\log R$.  The required estimate for the third summand is
    44	\[
    45	  a m^a 2^{-bm} \leq C'(\log R)^{-b},
    46	\]
    47	for a constant $C'$ depending only on $a$ and $b$.  This estimate, together
    48	with the source bounds for the first two summands, gives the asserted
    49	polylogarithmic bound for $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}$.
    50	
    51	\section{The source comparison}
    52	
    53	The proof of the canonical-parameter bound in \cite{Ji2020MIPStar} replaces
    54	$2^{-bmd}$ by $q^{-b}$ using the assertion $k\leq m$.%
    55	\footnote{Tracked in
    56	\href{https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/issues/16}{GitHub issue \#16}.
    57	The canonical parameter definition is at
    58	\path{references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex},
    59	lines~1503--1520; the bound and its proof are at lines~1521--1547, with the
    60	disputed comparison at lines~1535--1536.}

    62	the allowed values $a=1$ and $b=1/2$ give $c=4$, and $R=5$ gives $k=9$ but
    63	$m=8$.  Thus the displayed justification is false even though the lemma's
    64	conclusion remains valid.

    66	The third term can instead be bounded independently of $q$.  Since $d=1$ and
    67	$m\geq (c/2)\log R\geq\log R$,
    68	\[
    69	  2^{-bm}\leq R^{-b}.
    70	\]

    78	to zero as $R$ tends to infinity.  Absorbing its supremum into the universal

    94	third soundness term directly and proves the same final estimate after enlarging

     6	This file defines the tensor and reindexing operations used to transport states
     7	and operators in the Pauli basis test
     8	(`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`; paper
     9	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).

    18	/-- Conjugation by the local isometries in `thm:ms-rigidity` and
    19	`lem:pauli-binary`; blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403` and
    20	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:675-708`, paper `08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`. -/
    21	noncomputable def conjIsometry {ι ι' : Type*}
    22	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
    23	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι')
    24	    (M : Op ι) : Op ι' :=
    25	  let U : Matrix ι' ι ℂ := Matrix.toEuclideanLin.symm φ.toLinearMap
    26	  U * M * Uᴴ
    27	
    28	/-- Coordinate transport used by `def:strategy-distance`, blueprint
    29	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:212-219`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:273-285`. -/
    30	noncomputable def reindexState {ι ι' : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    31	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι'] (e : ι ≃ ι')
    32	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι' :=
    33	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι' ℂ).symm
    34	    (fun j => (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ ψ) (e.symm j))
    35	
    36	/-- Apply the two independent local isometries of `thm:ms-rigidity`; blueprint
    37	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper
    38	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`. -/
    39	noncomputable def isometryTensor
    40	    {ιA ιB κA κB : Type*}
    41	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    42	    [Fintype κA] [DecidableEq κA] [Fintype κB] [DecidableEq κB]
    43	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κA)
    44	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κB)
    45	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
    46	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (κA × κB) :=
    47	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv (κA × κB) ℂ).symm
    48	    (fun p =>
    49	      ∑ i : ιA, ∑ j : ιB,
    50	        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv κA ℂ)
    51	            (φA ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ιA ℂ).symm (Pi.single i 1))) p.1) *
    52	          ((EuclideanSpace.equiv κB ℂ)
    53	            (φB ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ιB ℂ).symm (Pi.single j 1))) p.2) *
    54	          ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA × ιB) ℂ) ψ (i, j)))

    56	/-- Coordinate tensor used in the ideal state of `thm:ms-rigidity`; blueprint
    57	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper
    58	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`. -/
    59	noncomputable def vecTensor {ι κ : Type*}
    60	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ]
    61	    (u : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ κ) :
    62	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × κ) :=
    63	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv (ι × κ) ℂ).symm
    64	    (fun p => (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ u) p.1 * (EuclideanSpace.equiv κ ℂ v) p.2)
    65	
    66	/-- Operator transport used by `def:strategy-distance`, blueprint
    67	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:212-219`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:273-285`. -/
    68	def reindexOp {ι ι' : Type*} (e : ι ≃ ι') (M : Op ι') : Op ι :=
    69	  (Matrix.reindex e.symm e.symm) M
    70	
    71	/-- Four-factor tensor shuffle used by `thm:ms-rigidity`; blueprint
    72	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper
    73	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`. -/
    74	def prodShuffle {α β γ δ : Type*} :
    75	    (α × β) × (γ × δ) ≃ (α × γ) × (β × δ) where
    76	  toFun p := ((p.1.1, p.2.1), (p.1.2, p.2.2))
    77	  invFun p := ((p.1.1, p.2.1), (p.1.2, p.2.2))
    78	  left_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    79	  right_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    80

    30	  ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ x y, 0 < x → 0 < y →

    20	noncomputable def Distribution.prod {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    21	    (μ : Distribution α) (ν : Distribution β) : Distribution (α × β) where
    22	  support := μ.support.product ν.support
    23	  weight p := μ.weight p.1 * ν.weight p.2
    24	  nonnegative p := mul_nonneg (μ.nonnegative p.1) (ν.nonnegative p.2)
    25	  outsideSupport p hp := by
    26	    by_cases hμ : p.1 ∈ μ.support
    27	    · have hν : p.2 ∉ ν.support := by
    28	        intro h
    29	        exact hp (Finset.mem_product.mpr ⟨hμ, h⟩)
    30	      simp [ν.outsideSupport p.2 hν]
    31	    · simp [μ.outsideSupport p.1 hμ]

    46	noncomputable def Distribution.mix {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
    47	    (t : ℝ) (ht0 : 0 ≤ t) (ht1 : t ≤ 1)
    48	    (μ ν : Distribution α) : Distribution α where
    49	  support := μ.support ∪ ν.support
    50	  weight a := t * μ.weight a + (1 - t) * ν.weight a
    51	  nonnegative a := by
    52	    exact add_nonneg
    53	      (mul_nonneg ht0 (μ.nonnegative a))
    54	      (mul_nonneg (sub_nonneg.mpr ht1) (ν.nonnegative a))
    55	  outsideSupport a ha := by
    56	    have hμ : a ∉ μ.support := fun h => ha (Finset.mem_union_left _ h)
    57	    have hν : a ∉ ν.support := fun h => ha (Finset.mem_union_right _ h)
    58	    simp [μ.outsideSupport a hμ, ν.outsideSupport a hν]

    62	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:544-626`. -/
    63	theorem Distribution.mix_isProbability {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
    64	    (t : ℝ) (μ ν : Distribution α) (hμ : μ.IsProbability)
    65	    (hν : ν.IsProbability) (ht0 : 0 ≤ t) (ht1 : t ≤ 1) :
    66	    (Distribution.mix t ht0 ht1 μ ν).IsProbability := by

    71	`05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:236-286`. -/
    72	noncomputable def Distribution.bind {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    73	    (μ : Distribution α) (ν : α → Distribution β) : Distribution β where
    74	  support := μ.support.biUnion (fun a => (ν a).support)
    75	  weight b := ∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a * (ν a).weight b
    76	  nonnegative b := Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => mul_nonneg (μ.nonnegative a) ((ν a).nonnegative b)

    78	    apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
    79	    intro a ha
    80	    have hnot : b ∉ (ν a).support := by
    81	      intro h
    82	      exact hb (Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨a, ha, h⟩)
    83	    simp [ν a |>.outsideSupport b hnot]

 # Pauli basis test soundness
 
 The quantitative error function and the source-shaped soundness statement live
 here.  All analytic estimates are intentionally proof-level obligations in the
 stage-4.1 skeleton; the carriers below are concrete finite-dimensional vectors
 and matrices so that later proofs can use the existing Hilbert-space API.
 
 ## References
 
 The main declaration is `thm:pauli` in
 `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, with paper origin
 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
 The distance functionals use `def:state-distance` and `def:povm-distance` from
 `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-220`.
 -/
 
 open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder

 /-- The Pauli-test error scale.  The argument order is `(a, b, ε, m, d, q)`;
 the powers are real `rpow`s and the asymptotic constants are absorbed into `a`,
 as specified by `thm:pauli` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`,
 paper `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
 -/
 noncomputable def deltaQld (a b ε : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
   a * Real.rpow ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) a *
     (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
       Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))

130	def evalPolyTupleAt {L : LdParams} (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)
   131	    (g : PolyTuple L) : Fin L.k → ScalarQ L :=
   132	  fun j => MvPolynomial.eval u (g j).1
   133	
   134	/-- Embed a geometric point into the ambient coefficient space used by a
   135	point question. -/
   136	def pointSpaceOf (L : LdParams) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) : LdSpace L :=
   137	  fun i => match i with
   138	  | .inl (.inl j) => u j
   139	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   140	  | .inr _ => 0
   141	
   142	/-- The typed low-degree point question associated with `u`. -/
   143	def ldPointQuestionOf (L : LdParams) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) : LdQuestion L :=
   144	  (.point, pointSpaceOf L u)
   145	
   146	/-- The quantitative error function in `lem:ld-soundness`.  Its argument order
   147	is `(a, b, ε, q, m, d, k)`. -/
   148	noncomputable def deltaLd (a b ε : ℝ) (q m d k : ℕ) : ℝ :=
   149	  a * Real.rpow (((d * m * k : ℕ) : ℝ)) a *
   150	    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
   151	      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))
   152	
   153	/-- Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low individual degree
   154	test (`lem:ld-soundness`, blueprint lines 125--178; paper theorem and proof
   155	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:413-458`).
   156	
   157	The first two consistency bounds compare the point-value outcomes of the
   158	strategy directly with evaluations of the polynomial measurements.
   159	
   160	The source reduction still requires proofs of the claimed game correspondence
   161	and of the auxiliary parameter bound. These two open facts are detailed in
   162	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex` and
   163	`rem:ld-soundness-provider`, and are tracked by issue #16. -/
   164	theorem exists_ld_soundness :
   165	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧
   166	      ∀ (L : LdParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε →
   167	        ∀ S : Strategy (ldGame L), S.IsProjective → 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
   168	          ∃ GA : PolyMeasTuple L S.ιA, ∃ GB : PolyMeasTuple L S.ιB,
   169	            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))
   170	                (fun u outcome =>
   171	                  heteroKron
   172	                    ((S.A (ldPointQuestionOf L u)).effect (.pointVals outcome)) 1)
   173	                (fun u outcome =>
   174	                  heteroKron 1
   175	                    ((GB.postprocess (evalPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome))
   176	                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k ∧
   177	            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))
   178	                (fun u outcome =>
   179	                  heteroKron
   180	                    ((GA.postprocess (evalPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome) 1)
   181	                (fun u outcome =>
   182	                  heteroKron 1
   183	                    ((S.B (ldPointQuestionOf L u)).effect (.pointVals outcome)))
   184	                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k ∧
   185	            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
   186	                (fun _ g => heteroKron (GA.effect g) 1)
   187	                (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 (GB.effect g))
   188	                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k := by
   189	  sorry

     4	/-!
     5	# Qubit form of Pauli basis test soundness
     6	
     7	The fixed self-dual normal basis converts the qudit EPR register and generalized
     8	Pauli projectors into qubit coordinates. The conversion uses only the basis
     9	stored in the canonical `FixedFieldModel`.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The conversion is `lem:pauli-binary` in
    14	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:675-708`, from
    15	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1163-1208`. The resulting
    16	`cor:pauli-binary` is in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:409-435`,
    17	from `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1450-1501`.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	open scoped BigOperators Matrix
    21	
    22	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    23	
    24	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
    25	
    26	noncomputable section
    27	
    28	/-- The bit register obtained by expanding every Pauli-register field element
    29	in the basis stored by `P.model`. -/
    30	abbrev QubitRegister (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
    31	  Cube P.m × Fin P.model.basisDim → ZMod 2
    32	
    33	/-- The ideal auxiliary state tensored with the qubit EPR register, in the
    34	local-player ordering used by `cor:pauli-binary`. -/
    35	noncomputable def idealQubitState (P : AdmissibleParams)
    36	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    37	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    38	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')) :
    39	    EuclideanSpace ℂ
    40	      ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
    41	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv
    42	      ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) ℂ).symm
    43	    (fun p =>
    44	      (EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA' × ιB') ℂ aux (p.1.1, p.2.1)) *
    45	        (EuclideanSpace.equiv (QubitRegister P × QubitRegister P) ℂ
    46	          (eprState (QubitRegister P)) (p.1.2, p.2.2)))
    47	
    48	/-- The local isometries, auxiliary spaces, and unit auxiliary state in
    49	`cor:pauli-binary`; this structure introduces no hypothesis beyond the paper
    50	theorem. -/
    51	structure QubitSoundnessWitness (P : AdmissibleParams)
    52	    (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)) where
    53	  ιA' : Type
    54	  ιB' : Type
    55	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA']
    56	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB']
    57	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA']
    58	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB']
    59	  φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
    60	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × QubitRegister P)
    61	  φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
    62	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × QubitRegister P)
    63	  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')
    64	  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1
    65	
    66	attribute [instance] QubitSoundnessWitness.ιAFintype
    67	  QubitSoundnessWitness.ιBFintype QubitSoundnessWitness.ιADecidableEq
    68	  QubitSoundnessWitness.ιBDecidableEq
    69	
    70	/-- Alice's ideal qubit projector placed on the joint target space. -/
    71	noncomputable def qubitProjOnA'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
    72	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    73	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
    74	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
    75	    Op ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
    76	  fun p q =>
    77	    if p.1.1 = q.1.1 ∧ p.2 = q.2 then
    78	      qubitPauliProj W (kappaVec P.model u) p.1.2 q.1.2
    79	    else 0
    80	
    81	/-- Bob's ideal qubit projector placed on the joint target space. -/
    82	noncomputable def qubitProjOnB'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
    83	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    84	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
    85	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
    86	    Op ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
    87	  fun p q =>
    88	    if p.1 = q.1 ∧ p.2.1 = q.2.1 then

    90	    else 0
    91	
    92	/-- Lift a conjugated Alice effect to the full qubit target space. -/
    93	noncomputable def liftedQubitAEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
    94	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    95	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    96	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
    97	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × QubitRegister P))
    98	    (M : Op S.ιA) :
    99	    Op ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
   100	  heteroKron (conjIsometry φA M) 1
   101	
   102	/-- Lift a conjugated Bob effect to the full qubit target space. -/
   103	noncomputable def liftedQubitBEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   104	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   105	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   106	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   107	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × QubitRegister P))
   108	    (M : Op S.ιB) :
   109	    Op ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
   110	  heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB M)
   111	
   112	/-- Alice's qubit-projector family distance in `cor:pauli-binary`. -/
   113	noncomputable def qubitOperatorDistanceA
   114	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   115	    (w : QubitSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   116	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   117	    ‖applyOperatorToState
   118	      (liftedQubitAEffect S w.φA
   119	          ((S.A (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   120	        qubitProjOnA'' P W u)
   121	      (idealQubitState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   122	
   123	/-- Bob's qubit-projector family distance in `cor:pauli-binary`. -/
   124	noncomputable def qubitOperatorDistanceB
   125	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   126	    (w : QubitSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   127	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   128	    ‖applyOperatorToState
   129	      (liftedQubitBEffect S w.φB
   130	          ((S.B (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   131	        qubitProjOnB'' P W u)
   132	      (idealQubitState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   133	
   134	/-- `cor:pauli-binary`: soundness of the Pauli basis test in qubit
   135	coordinates. Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:409-435`, paper
   136	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1450-1501`.
   137	
   138	The theorem retains the source-compatible nonnegative error boundary and uses
   139	only `P.model` and its stored basis dimension. -/
   140	theorem pauli_soundness_qubit :
   141	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b < 1 ∧
   142	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε →
   143	        ∀ S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P), 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
   144	          ∃ w : QubitSoundnessWitness P S,
   145	            ‖isometryTensor w.φA w.φB S.ψ - idealQubitState P w.aux‖ ≤
   146	                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ∧
   147	            (∀ W : PauliKind,
   148	              qubitOperatorDistanceA P S w W ≤
   149	                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) ∧
   150	            ∀ W : PauliKind,
   151	              qubitOperatorDistanceB P S w W ≤
   152	                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q := by
   153	  sorry
   154	
   155	end
   156	
   157	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

650	\begin{proof}
   651	 	A proof of the rigidity of the Magic Square game can be found in~\cite[Theorem 6.9]{coladangelo2017robust}. There are a couple minor differences between their rigidity statement and the one stated here. First, they state that the robustness of the Magic Square self-test is $O(\eps)$; however they specify the closeness between the actual and ideal states in terms of the trace norm, whereas we specify the closeness between $\phi_\alice \otimes \phi_\bob \ket{\psi}$ and $\ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes 2}\otimes \ket{\aux}$ in terms of the Euclidean distance, which translates to $O(\sqrt{\eps})$ instead of $O(\eps)$. Second, their choice of ideal strategy specifies that the observables corresponding to $\Variable_1$ and $\Variable_5$ questions are $I \otimes \sigma^Z$ and $\sigma^{Z} \sigma^{X} \otimes \sigma^Z \sigma^X$; however under a local change of basis these are equivalent to $\sigma^X \otimes I$ and $\sigma^Z \otimes I$ respectively.
   652	\end{proof}
   653	
   654	We will need the following theorem,
   655	which shows that any pair of anticommuting observables 
   656	can be used to form a value-$1$ strategy for the Magic Square game.
   657	
   658	\begin{theorem}
   659	  \label{thm:ms-from-ac}
   660	  Let $A = \{A_b\}_{b \in \F_2}$ and $B = \{B_b\}_{b \in \F_2}$ be two-outcome
   661	  projective measurements acting on $(\C^q)^{\otimes n}$ which are consistent on
   662	  $\ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes n}$, and let $\mathcal{O}_A = A_0 - A_1$ and
   663	  $\mathcal{O}_B = B_0 - B_1$ be the corresponding observables.
   664	  Suppose that $\mathcal{O}_A \mathcal{O}_B = -\mathcal{O}_B \mathcal{O}_A$.
   665	  Then there exists a symmetric strategy $\strategy = (\psi, M)$ for the Magic
   666	  Square game with the following properties.
   667	  \begin{enumerate}
   668	  \item $\strategy$ is an SPCC strategy of value $1$.
   669	  \item The state $\ket{\psi}$ has the form $\ket{\psi} = \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes
   670	      n} \otimes \ket{\EPR_2}$.
   671	  \item For $b \in \{0,1\}$, we have $M^{\Variable_1}_b = A_b \otimes I$ and
   672	    $M^{\Variable_5}_b = B_b \otimes I$.\label{item:embeds}
   673	  \end{enumerate}
   674	\end{theorem}
   675	
   676	\begin{proof}
   677	  The strategy~$\strategy$ is based on the canonical two-qubit strategy for the
   678	  Magic Square game as described in, for example,~\cite{aravind2002simple}.
   679	  The state is $\ket{\psi} = \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes n} \otimes \ket{\EPR_2}$.
   680	  We specify the measurements of~$\strategy$ in
   681	  Figure~\ref{fig:ms-operator-soln} as an \emph{operator solution} for the Magic
   682	  Square game, meant to be read as follows: each cell contains a two-outcome
   683	  projective measurement $\{E_0, E_1\}$ on $(\C^q)^{\otimes n} \otimes \C^2$
   684	  written as its \emph{$\pm 1$-valued observable} $E_0 - E_1$.
   685	  When Player~$\alice$ or~$\bob$ receives the question $\Variable_j$ for $j \in
   686	  \{1, \ldots, 9\}$, they measure their share of~$\ket{\psi}$ using the
   687	  measurement specified by the cell corresponding to~$\Variable_j$ and receive a
   688	  single-bit measurement.
   689	  When they receive the question $\Constraint_i$ for $i \in \{1,2,\ldots,6\}$,
   690	  they simultaneously perform the three measurements in the corresponding row or
   691	  column on $\ket{\psi}$ to obtain three bits.
   692	  For example, if Player~$\alice$ receives question~$\Variable_1$, they
   693	  measure~$\ket{\psi}$ using the measurement $\{A_0 \otimes I, A_1 \otimes I\}$
   694	  corresponding to the observable $\cal{O}_A \otimes I$ (where the first
   695	  operator acts on $\ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes n}$ and the second acts on
   696	  $\ket{\EPR_2}$).
   697	  Similarly, on question~$\Variable_5$, they use the measurement $\{B_0 \otimes
   698	  I, B_1 \otimes I\}$.
   699	  This establishes Item~\ref{item:embeds} of the theorem.

  1229	We describe an honest, value-$1$ PCC strategy for the Pauli basis test.
  1230	
  1231	
  1232	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:pauli-completeness}
  1233	  The Pauli basis test $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ has a value-$1$ SPCC strategy.
  1234	\end{lemma}
  1235	
  1236	\begin{proof}
  1237	  We begin by specifying the value-$1$ strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, E)$.
  1238	  The state is
  1239	  \begin{equation*}
  1240	    \ket{\psi} = \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes M} \otimes \ket{\EPR_2}\;.
  1241	  \end{equation*}
  1242	  Now we specify the measurements.
  1243	  We start with measurements associated with questions of type $\Point$,
  1244	  $\ALine$, $\DLine$, and $\Pauli$.
  1245	  Using notation introduced in Section~\ref{sec:ld-encoding}, for $W \in \{X,
  1246	  Z\}$,
  1247	  \begin{align*}
  1248	    E^{(\Point,W),\, y}_{\, a}
  1249	    & = \tau^W_{[g_{\cdot}(y) = a]} \otimes I\;,\\
  1250	    E^{(\ALine,W),\, \line}_{\, f}
  1251	    & = \tau^W_{[(g_{\cdot})|_\line = f]} \otimes I\;,\\
  1252	    E^{(\DLine,W),\, \line}_{\, f}
  1253	    & = \tau^W_{[(g_{\cdot})|_\line = f]} \otimes I\;,\\    
  1254	    E^{(\Pauli,W)}_{\, a}
  1255	    & = \tau^W_{a} \otimes I\;.
  1256	  \end{align*}
  1257	  Here, the bracket notation used to post-process measurement outcomes is
  1258	  defined in \Cref{def:bracket}.
  1259	  Thus, for example, the measurement on question $((\Point,W),y)$ corresponds to
  1260	  first performing the measurement $\{\tau^W_h\}_{h \in \F_q^M}$, receiving an
  1261	  outcome $h \in \F_q^M$, and then outputting the value $a = g_{h}(y)$.
  1262	
  1263	  For $\ALine$ and $\DLine$ questions, the question content $\line$ denotes
  1264	  either an axis-parallel line $\line(u_0,e_i)$ for some $i \in
  1265	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$, or a diagonal line $\line(u_0,v')$ for some $v' \in
  1266	  \F_q^m$.
  1267	  As described at the beginning of \Cref{sec:qld-game}, axis-parallel lines are
  1268	  specified by pairs $(u_0,s) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q$ and diagonal lines are
  1269	  specified by triples $(u_0,s,v) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q \times \F_q^m$.
  1270	  The measurement on question $((\ALine,W),\line)$, for example, corresponds to
  1271	  first performing the measurement $\{\tau^W_h\}_{h \in \F_q^M}$ to get an
  1272	  outcome $h \in \F_q^M$, and reporting the univariate polynomial $f_\line(t) =
  1273	  g_{h}(u_0 + te_i)$ where $\line$ is specified by $(u_0,s)$ and $i = \chi(s)$.
  1274	  
  1275	
  1276	
  1277	  Next we specify the POVMs associated with questions of type $\Constraint$,
  1278	  $\Variable$, and $\Pair$.
  1279	  Questions with these question types have a question content that is a tuple
  1280	  $\omega= (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)\in (\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q^2$.
  1281	  Given such a tuple, consider the two $\F_2$-valued POVMs $A=\{A_b\}_{b \in
  1282	    \F_2}$ and $B=\{B_b\}_{b \in \F_2}$ defined as
  1283	  \begin{align}
  1284	    A_b & = \tau^X_{[\tr(g_{\cdot}(u_X)\, r_\xpt) = b]} \otimes I\;,\label{eq:gonna-expand-A}\\
  1285	    B_b & = \tau^Z_{[\tr(g_{\cdot}(u_Z)\, r_\zpt) = b]} \otimes I\;.\label{eq:gonna-expand-B}
  1286	  \end{align}
  1287	  We would like to determine when the two observables $\mathcal{O}_A = A_0 -
  1288	  A_1$ and $\mathcal{O}_B = B_0 - B_1$ commute or anti-commute.
  1289	  Towards this we derive alternative expressions for these observables from
  1290	  which their commutativity becomes plain from inspection.
  1291	  We begin by inspecting the first matrices on the right-hand sides of
  1292	  Equations~\eqref{eq:gonna-expand-A} and~\eqref{eq:gonna-expand-B}:
  1293	  \begin{align}
  1294	  \tau^W_{[\tr(g_{\cdot}(u_W)\, r_W) = b]}
  1295	  &= \sum_{h : \tr(g_{h}(u_W)\, r_W) = b} \tau^W_h\nonumber\\
  1296	  &= \sum_{h : \tr((h\, \cdot\, \ind_{m}(u_W)) \cdot r_W ) = b} \tau^W_h\;,\label{eq:expand-with-dot-product}
  1297	  \end{align}
  1298	  where~\eqref{eq:expand-with-dot-product}
  1299	  follows by  Definition~\ref{eq:low-degree-encoding-definition}.
  1300	  As a result,
  1301	  \begin{align}
  1302	&  \tau^W_{[\tr(g_{\cdot}(u_W)\, r_W) = 0]}
  1303	  -   \tau^W_{[\tr(g_{\cdot}(u_W)\, r_W) = 1]} \notag \\
  1304	  & = \sum_{h : \tr((h\, \cdot\, \ind_{m}(u_W)) \cdot r_W ) = 0} \tau^W_h
  1305	  	- \sum_{h : \tr((h\, \cdot\, \ind_{m}(u_W)) \cdot r_W ) = 1} \tau^W_h\nonumber\\
  1306	  & = \sum_{h} (-1)^{\tr((h\, \cdot\, \ind_{m}(u_W)) \cdot r_W )} \tau^W_h\nonumber\\
  1307	  & = \tau^W(\ind_{m}(u_W)r_W)\;,\label{eq:finally-got-an-observable}
  1308	  \end{align}
  1309	  where the last step uses~\eqref{eq:pauli-obs-proj}.
  1310	  As a result, Equation~\eqref{eq:finally-got-an-observable}
  1311	  and Equations~\eqref{eq:gonna-expand-A} and~\eqref{eq:gonna-expand-B} imply that
  1312	  \begin{equation*}
  1313	  \mathcal{O}_A = \tau^X(\ind_{m}(u_X)r_X) \otimes I,\quad
  1314	  \mathcal{O}_B = \tau^Z(\ind_{m}(u_Z)r_Z) \otimes I\;.
  1315	  \end{equation*}
  1316	  Now, let $\gamma = \tr((\ind_{m}(u_X)r_X) \cdot (\ind_{m}(u_Z)r_Z)) \in \F_2$,
  1317	  as in Equation~\eqref{eq:gamma-value}.
  1318	  Then by Equation~\eqref{eq:twisted-fq},
  1319	  \begin{equation*}
  1320	  \mathcal{O}_A \mathcal{O}_B = (-1)^{\gamma} \mathcal{O}_B \mathcal{O}_A\;.
  1321	  \end{equation*}
  1322	  As a result, $\gamma$ quantifies whether the observables $\mathcal{O}_A$ and
  1323	  $\mathcal{O}_B$ commute, and therefore whether the measurements~$A$ and~$B$
  1324	  commute.
  1325	  If $\gamma = 0$, they commute.
  1326	  If $\gamma = 1$, they anti-commute.
  1327	  We now specify the POVMs associated with questions of type $\Constraint$,
  1328	  $\Variable$, and $\Pair$, considering separately the cases when $\gamma = 0$
  1329	  or $\gamma = 1$.
  1330	  \begin{enumerate}
  1331	  \item If $\gamma = 0$, 
  1332	     for each $\beta_X, \beta_Z \in \F_2$ define
  1333	    \begin{equation}\label{eq:pair-definition}
  1334	      E^{\Pair,\, \omega}_{\beta_X,\, \beta_Z} = A_{\beta_X} \cdot B_{\beta_Z}\;,
  1335	    \end{equation}
  1336	    \begin{equation*}
  1337	      E^{(\Pair,X),\, \omega}_{a} = A_{a} \;,\qquad
  1338	      E^{(\Pair,Z),\, \omega}_{a} = B_{a}\;.
  1339	    \end{equation*}
  1340	    The POVM associated with questions of type $\Constraint$ and $\Variable$ are
  1341	    defined to be trivial.
  1342	    In particular, we define
  1343	    \begin{equation*}
  1344	      E^{\Constraint_i,\, \omega}_{\, 0,\, 0,\, 0}
  1345	      = E^{\Variable_j,\, \omega}_{\, 0} = I\;,
  1346	    \end{equation*}
  1347	    and the remaining POVM elements in these measurements are set to be zero.
  1348	  \item If $\gamma = 1$, then $\mathcal{O}_A$ and $\mathcal{O}_B$ anti-commute.
  1349	    In this case we define measurements $E^{\Constraint_i,\, \omega}$ and
  1350	    $E^{\Variable_j,\, \omega}$, for all $i\in\{1,\ldots,6\}$ and $j
  1351	    \in\{1,\ldots,9\}$ to be those guaranteed by Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-from-ac}.
  1352	    Measurements associated with inputs of type $\Pair$ are defined to be
  1353	    trivial.
  1354	    In particular, we define
  1355	    \begin{equation*}
  1356	      E^{\Pair,\, \omega}_{0,\, 0} = E^{(\Pair,X),\, \omega}_{0} = E^{(\Pair,Z),\, \omega}_{0} = I\;,
  1357	    \end{equation*}
  1358	    and the remaining matrices in these measurements are set to be zero.
  1359	  \end{enumerate}
  1360	  This completes the specification of the strategy.
  1361	
  1362	  Now, we show that $\strategy$ is a value-$1$ SPCC strategy.
  1363	  It is clearly symmetric and projective. 
  1364	  To show that it is consistent, we note that all measurements are Pauli basis
  1365	  measurements, which are consistent, or measurements produced by
  1366	  Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-from-ac}, which are also consistent.
  1367	  The only exception is the $\Pair$ measurement in the $\gamma = 0$ case, which
  1368	  by Equation~\eqref{eq:pair-definition} is a product of two commuting,
  1369	  consistent measurements, and so it is therefore also consistent.
  1370	  To show that it is commuting, we note that for each $W \in \{X, Z\}$, all
  1371	  $(\Point, W)$, $(\ALine, W)$, $(\DLine,W)$ and $(\Pauli, W)$ measurements
  1372	  commute as they are all measurements in the Pauli~$W$ basis.
  1373	  Next, if $\gamma = 0$ then the $\Constraint$ and $\Variable$ measurements
  1374	  commute trivially, and for $W \in \{X, Z\}$, the $(\Point, W)$ measurement
  1375	  commutes with the $(\Pair, W)$ measurement, as they are both $W$ basis
  1376	  measurements, and the measurement $E^{\Pair, \omega}_{\beta_X, \, \beta_Z} =
  1377	  A_{\beta_X}\cdot B_{\beta_Z}$ commutes with $E^{(\Pair, W), \omega}_{a}$
  1378	  because $A$ and~$B$ commute.
  1379	  On the other hand, if $\gamma \neq 0$, then the $\Pair$ measurements commute
  1380	  trivially, and the $\Constraint$ and $\Variable$ measurements commute by
  1381	  Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-from-ac}.
  1382	  Finally, the $(\Point, X)$ measurement commutes with $\Variable_1$ because
  1383	  both are $X$-basis measurements, and likewise both $(\Point, Z)$ and
  1384	  $\Variable_5$ are $Z$-basis measurements.
  1385	  
  1386	  It remains to show that $\strategy$ is value-$1$.
  1387		Consider first the first three tests executed by the decision procedure in
  1388	  Figure~\ref{fig:decider_pauli}.
  1389	  The strategy passes the consistency checks with probability~$1$ because it is
  1390	  projective and consistent.
  1391	  It passes the low-degree checks because it answers those consistently with an
  1392	  honest strategy in the classical low-degree test.
  1393			
  1394	  Next, consider the remaining four tests.
  1395	  Fix an $\omega= (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)$ and~$\gamma$ as
  1396	  in~\eqref{eq:gamma-value}.
  1397	  If $\gamma = 0$, then the strategy passes the commutation check with
  1398	  probability~$1$ by construction.
  1399	  As for the consistency check in Item~\ref{item:commutation-consistency},
  1400	  we can write the $(\Point, W)$ measurement as follows: 
  1401	  \begin{equation*}
  1402	  E^{(\Point,W),\, y}_{[\tr(\,\cdot\, r_W) = a_{\overline{w}}]}
  1403	  = \tau^W_{[\tr(g_{\cdot}(y)r_W) = a_{\overline{w}}]} \otimes I
  1404	  = E^{(\Pair, W), \omega}_{a_{\overline{w}}} \otimes I.
  1405	  \end{equation*}
  1406	  As a result, due to the consistency of the $(\Pair, W)$ measurement, the
  1407	  consistency check is passed with probability~$1$.
  1408	  On the other hand, if $\gamma \neq 0$, then the strategy passes the Magic
  1409	  Square check by Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-from-ac}.
  1410	  As for the consistency check in Item~\ref{item:magic-square-consistency}, we
  1411	  can write the $(\Point, X)$ measurement as follows:
  1412	  \begin{equation*}
  1413	  E^{(\Point,X),\, y}_{[\tr(\,\cdot\, r_X) = a_{\overline{w}}]}
  1414	  = \tau^X_{[\tr(g_{\cdot}(y)r_X) = a_{\overline{w}}]} \otimes I
  1415	  = E^{\Variable_1,\, \omega}_{a_{\overline{w}}} \otimes I,
  1416	  \end{equation*}
  1417	  where the last step is by Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-from-ac}.
  1418	  As these measurements are consistent, this test is passed with
  1419	  probability~$1$.
  1420	\end{proof}

  1426	\paragraph{Soundness of the Pauli basis test.} 
  1427	We state the soundness properties of the Pauli basis test.
  1428	The following is an adaptation of the self-testing statement in~\cite[Theorem
  1429	6.4]{NW19}.
  1430	
  1431	\begin{theorem}
  1432	  \label{thm:pauli}
  1433	There exists a function 
  1434	\[\delta_{\qld}(\eps,m,d,q) = a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})\]
  1435	 for universal constants $a \geq 1$ and $0 < b < 1$ such that the following holds. For all admissible parameter tuples $\qldparams = (q,m,d)$ and for all strategies $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},A,B)$ for the game $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ that succeed with probability at least $1 - \eps$, there exist local isometries $\phi_\alice: \mH_\alice \to \mH_{\alice'} \otimes \mH_{\alice''},\phi_\bob: \mH_\bob \to \mH_{\bob'} \otimes \mH_{\bob''}$ (where $\ket{\psi} \in \mH_\alice \otimes \mH_\bob$ and $\mH_{\alice''},\mH_{\bob''} \cong (\C^q)^{\otimes M}$ with $M = 2^m$) and a state $\ket{\aux} \in \mH_{\alice'} \otimes \mH_{\bob'}$ such that 
  1436	\begin{enumerate}
  1437	    \item $\left \| \phi_\alice \otimes \phi_B \ket{\psi} - \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes M}  \right \| \leq \delta_{\qld}(\eps,m,d,q)$,
  1438	    \item Letting $\tilde{A}^x_a = \phi_A\, A^x_a \, \phi_A^\dagger$ and $\tilde{B}^y_b = \phi_B B^y_b \phi_B^\dagger$, we have for $W \in \{X,Z\}$
  1439	    \begin{gather*}
  1440	        \tilde{A}^{(\pauli,W)}_u \otimes I_{\bob'\bob''} \approx_{\delta_{\qld}} (\tau^W_u)_{\alice''} \otimes I_{\alice' \bob' \bob''} \\
  1441	        I_{\alice'\alice''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{(\pauli,W)}_u    \approx_{\delta_{\qld}} I_{\alice' \alice'' \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_u)_{\bob''}\;,
  1442	    \end{gather*}
  1443	    where the $\approx_{\delta_{\qld}}$ statement holds with respect to the state $\ket{\aux}_{\alice'\bob'} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes M}_{\alice''\bob''}$ and the answer summation is over $u \in \F_q^M$.
  1444	\end{enumerate}
  1445	\end{theorem}
  1446	
  1447	We provide a proof of \Cref{thm:pauli} in \Cref{sec:qld-analysis}.

  1450	The strategies described in the proof of \Cref{lem:pauli-completeness} and in the conclusion of \Cref{thm:pauli} are described in terms of qudit Pauli measurements and maximally entangled states defined over $q$-dimensional qudits. 
  1451	However, it is more convenient for our application of the Pauli basis test to
  1452	instead deal with \emph{qubits}.
  1453	In particular, we use the Pauli basis test in the ``introspection game'' of
  1454	Section~\ref{sec:introspection}, where the players are commanded to sample
  1455	questions according to a sampler $\sampler$ of a normal form verifier.

     6	
     7	The definitions here use finite matrix entries and rank-one projectors, so they
     8	are usable by the later game statements without introducing an abstract
     9	operator algebra.  The Fourier/orthogonality identities are retained as named
    10	proof obligations for subsequent stages.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	The source-facing nodes are `def:lin-reg`, `def:EPR`, `def:generalized-pauli`,
    15	and `lem:pauli-observable-expansion` in
    16	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:494-652`.  The paper origin is
    17	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:908-1161`.
    18	-/

    20	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    21	
    22	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    23	
    24	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    25	
    26	variable {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
    27	  [Algebra (ZMod 2) K]
    28	
    29	/-- The two generalized Pauli bases used by the test in `def:generalized-pauli`,
    30	blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`, paper origin
    31	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
    32	-/
    33	inductive PauliKind where
    34	  | X
    35	  | Z
    36	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    37	
    38	/-- The binary character used for generalized Pauli phases; see
    39	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1081`.
    40	
    41	It is public because the Fourier expansion declarations below expose this
    42	character in their statement types. -/
    43	noncomputable def phaseSign (t : ZMod 2) : ℂ :=
    44	  if t = 0 then 1 else -1
    45	
    46	/--
    47	The shift operator `τ^X(a)`.  Blueprint `def:generalized-pauli`,
    48	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`; paper origin
    49	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
    50	-/
    51	noncomputable def tauShift (a : K) : Op K :=
    52	  fun i j => if i = j + a then 1 else 0
    53	
    54	/--
    55	The phase operator `τ^Z(b)`, with the fixed binary trace in the phase.  It is
    56	the second operator of `def:generalized-pauli` (blueprint lines 529-571; paper
    57	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`).
    58	-/
    59	noncomputable def tauPhase (b : K) : Op K :=
    60	  fun i j => if i = j then phaseSign (binTrace K (b * j)) else 0
    61	
    62	/-- The single-qudit eigenvector coordinate used in the tensor-product basis;
    63	see `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1126-1161`. -/
    64	private noncomputable def singlePauliVec (W : PauliKind) (e x : K) : ℂ :=
    65	  match W with
    66	  | .Z => if x = e then 1 else 0
    67	  | .X =>
    68	      (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card K : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ * phaseSign (binTrace K (e * x))
    69	
    70	/--
    71	The normalized single/multi-qudit eigenvector for a Pauli basis label.  For an
    72	index type `ι`, the input `e : ι → K` labels the tensor-product basis vector.
    73	This is the vector form of `def:generalized-pauli`, blueprint
    74	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:550-570`, paper origin
    75	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1101-1122`.
    76	-/
    77	noncomputable def pauliVec {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    78	    (W : PauliKind) (e : ι → K) (x : ι → K) : ℂ :=
    79	  ∏ i : ι, singlePauliVec W (e i) (x i)
    80	
    81	/--
    82	The rank-one projector onto `pauliVec W e`.  This is the projective measurement
    83	element `τ^W_e` in `def:generalized-pauli` (blueprint lines 562-570; paper
    84	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1101-1122`).
    85	-/
    86	noncomputable def pauliProj {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    87	    (W : PauliKind) (e : ι → K) : Op (ι → K) :=
    88	  Matrix.vecMulVec (pauliVec W e) (fun x => star (pauliVec W e x))
    89	
    90	/-- A compact operator-valued form of a generalized Pauli observable from
    91	`def:generalized-pauli`, blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`, paper origin
    92	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
    93	-/
    94	noncomputable def tauObservable {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    95	    (W : PauliKind) (a : ι → K) : Op (ι → K) :=
    96	  fun x y =>
    97	    ∏ i : ι,
    98	      match W with
    99	      | .X => tauShift (a i) (x i) (y i)
   100	      | .Z => tauPhase (a i) (x i) (y i)
   101	
   102	/--
   103	The EPR vector on a finite label space.  Blueprint `def:EPR`,
   104	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:513-523`; paper origin
   105	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`.
   106	-/
   107	noncomputable def eprState (V : Type*) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Nonempty V] :
   108	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (V × V) :=
   109	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv (V × V) ℂ).symm
   110	    (fun p : V × V =>
   111	      if p.1 = p.2 then (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card V : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ else 0)
   112	
   113	/-- The EPR vector is normalized on a nonempty finite carrier; see
   114	`def:EPR`, `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`. -/
   115	theorem eprState_norm (V : Type*) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Nonempty V] :
   116	    ‖eprState V‖ = 1 := by
   117	  sorry
   118	
   119	/--
   120	Fourier expansion of a generalized Pauli observable in the Pauli projectors.
   121	This is `lem:pauli-observable-expansion`, equations `eq:pauli-obs-proj` and
   122	`eq:pauli-inversion-0`, in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:638-652`;
   123	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1141-1161`.
   124	Both directions are deliberately left as proof-level obligations in stage 4.1.
   125	-/
   126	theorem tauObservable_eq_sum_pauliProj {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   127	    (W : PauliKind) (a : ι → K) :
   128	    tauObservable W a =
   129	      ∑ e : ι → K, phaseSign (binTrace K (dotProduct a e)) • pauliProj W e := by
   130	  sorry
   131	
   132	/-- The inverse Fourier expansion of a Pauli projector
   133	(`lem:pauli-observable-expansion`), blueprint
   134	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:638-652`, paper origin
   135	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1141-1161`.
   136	-/
   137	theorem pauliProj_eq_avg_tauObservable {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   138	    (W : PauliKind) (e : ι → K) :
   139	    pauliProj W e =
   140	      (Fintype.card (ι → K) : ℂ)⁻¹ •
   141	        ∑ a : ι → K, phaseSign (binTrace K (dotProduct a e)) • tauObservable W a := by
   142	  sorry

     7	# Finite fields and Fourier orthogonality
     8	
     9	This file formalizes the finite-field trace and the two Fourier orthogonality facts
    10	from `references/ldt-paper/preliminaries.tex` (lines 15–83).
    11	
    12	## Main results
    13	
    14	* `fourier_fact_scalar` (`prop:fourier-fact-scalar`):
    15	  `𝔼_{x ∈ 𝔽_q} ω^{tr[x·a]} = 1 if a = 0, 0 otherwise`
    16	* `fourier_fact_vector` (`prop:fourier-fact-vector`):
    17	  Vector version over `𝔽_q^m`.

    19	## References

    24	open scoped BigOperators

    26	namespace MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries

    28	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    29	
    30	section Trace
    31	
    32	variable {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
    33	variable {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F] [Algebra (ZMod p) F]
    34	
    35	/-- Paper label `def:finite-field-trace`.
    36	
    37	The finite-field trace `F → F_p`, implemented as Mathlib's algebraic trace
    38	`Algebra.trace (ZMod p) F`. -/
    39	noncomputable abbrev ffTrace : F → ZMod p :=
    40	  Algebra.trace (ZMod p) F
    41	
    42	/-- Paper label `def:finite-field-trace`.
    43	
    44	After applying the prime-field inclusion, `ffTrace` agrees with the paper's
    45	Frobenius-sum formula. -/
    46	theorem algebraMap_ffTrace_eq_sum_pow (x : F) :
    47	    algebraMap (ZMod p) F (ffTrace (p := p) (F := F) x) =
    48	      ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (Module.finrank (ZMod p) F), x ^ (p ^ i) := by
    49	  simpa [ffTrace, Nat.card_zmod] using
    50	    (FiniteField.algebraMap_trace_eq_sum_pow (K := ZMod p) (L := F) x)
    51	
    52	section Honest
    53	
    54	variable (params : Parameters) (spec : PrimePowerFieldSpec params)
    55	
    56	local instance : Fact spec.p.Prime := ⟨spec.pPrime⟩
    57	
    58	/-- Paper label `def:finite-field-trace`.
    59	
    60	For the honest finite field `F_q = GF(p^t)`, `ffTrace` is the Frobenius sum
    61	`∑_{ℓ=0}^{t-1} x^(p^ℓ)` from the paper. -/
    62	theorem honestFq_algebraMap_ffTrace_eq_sum_pow (x : HonestFq params spec) :
    63	    algebraMap (ZMod spec.p) (HonestFq params spec)
    64	        (ffTrace (p := spec.p) (F := HonestFq params spec) x) =
    65	      ∑ i ∈ Finset.range spec.n, x ^ (spec.p ^ i) := by
    66	  simpa [ffTrace, HonestFq, GaloisField.finrank (p := spec.p) spec.nPos.ne', Nat.card_zmod]
    67	    using
    68	      (FiniteField.algebraMap_trace_eq_sum_pow
    69	        (K := ZMod spec.p) (L := HonestFq params spec) x)

    74	section Fourier
    75	
    76	-- The Fourier section uses `[Fintype F]` (rather than `[Finite F]` as in the Trace section)
    77	-- because `AddChar.expect_eq_ite` requires a `Fintype` instance. Downstream users with
    78	-- only `[Finite F]` can obtain `Fintype` via `Fintype.ofFinite`.
    79	variable {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
    80	variable {F : Type*} [Field F] [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] [Algebra (ZMod p) F]
    81	
    82	/-- The canonical complex additive character `x ↦ ω^{tr[x]}` on `F`. -/
    83	noncomputable abbrev ffChar : AddChar F ℂ :=
    84	  (ZMod.stdAddChar (N := p)).compAddMonoidHom (Algebra.trace (ZMod p) F).toAddMonoidHom
    85	
    86	omit [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] in
    87	@[simp] theorem ffChar_apply (x : F) :
    88	    ffChar (p := p) (F := F) x =
    89	      ZMod.stdAddChar (N := p) (ffTrace (p := p) (F := F) x) :=
    90	  rfl
    91	
    92	omit [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] in
    93	private theorem ffTrace_nondegenerate [Finite F] (a : F) (ha : a ≠ 0) :
    94	    ∃ b : F, ffTrace (p := p) (F := F) (a * b) ≠ 0 := by
    95	  haveI : CharP F p := (Algebra.charP_iff (ZMod p) F p).mp (ZMod.charP p)
    96	  have hp : p = ringChar F := by
    97	    simpa using (ringChar.eq F p).symm
    98	  subst p
    99	  simpa [ffTrace] using (FiniteField.trace_to_zmod_nondegenerate F (a := a) ha)
   100	
   101	omit [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] in
   102	private theorem ffChar_ne_zero [Finite F] : ffChar (p := p) (F := F) ≠ 0 := by
   103	  rw [AddChar.ne_zero_iff]
   104	  obtain ⟨a, ha0⟩ :=
   105	    ffTrace_nondegenerate (p := p) (F := F) (a := (1 : F)) one_ne_zero
   106	  have ha : ffTrace (p := p) (F := F) a ≠ 0 := by
   107	    simpa using ha0
   108	  refine ⟨a, ?_⟩
   109	  rw [ffChar_apply]
   110	  intro h
   111	  exact ha ((AddChar.IsPrimitive.zmod_char_eq_one_iff p (ZMod.isPrimitive_stdAddChar p) _).mp h)
   112	
   113	/-- Paper label `prop:fourier-fact-scalar`.
   114	
   115	The Fourier orthogonality relation for the finite field `F`: the expectation
   116	of the additive character `ω^{tr[x·a]}` over `x ∈ F` equals `1` when `a = 0`
   117	and `0` otherwise. -/
   118	theorem fourier_fact_scalar (a : F) :
   119	    𝔼 x : F, ffChar (p := p) (F := F) (x * a) =
   120	      if a = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 := by
   121	  let ψ : AddChar F ℂ := (ffChar (p := p) (F := F)).mulShift a
   122	  calc
   123	    𝔼 x : F, ffChar (p := p) (F := F) (x * a) = 𝔼 x : F, ψ x := by
   124	      simp [ψ, AddChar.mulShift_apply, mul_comm]
   125	    _ = if ψ = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 := AddChar.expect_eq_ite ψ
   126	    _ = if a = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 := by
   127	      by_cases ha : a = 0
   128	      · have hψ : ψ = 0 := by
   129	          ext x
   130	          simp [ψ, ha]
   131	        simp [ha, hψ]
   132	      · have hψ : ψ ≠ 0 := by
   133	          have hprimitive : (ffChar (p := p) (F := F)).IsPrimitive := by
   134	            exact AddChar.IsPrimitive.of_ne_one (by
   135	              simpa [AddChar.one_eq_zero] using (ffChar_ne_zero (p := p) (F := F)))
   136	          simpa [ψ, AddChar.one_eq_zero] using hprimitive ha
   137	        simp [ha, hψ]
   138	
   139	section Vector
   140	
   141	variable {m : ℕ}
   142	
   143	-- We define `ffDotProduct` directly rather than reusing `Matrix.dotProduct` to avoid
   144	-- pulling in the full `Mathlib.Data.Matrix.Basic` import. The definitions are identical.
   145	/-- The standard dot product on `F^m`. -/
   146	def ffDotProduct (u v : Fin m → F) : F :=
   147	  ∑ i, u i * v i
   148	
   149	/-- The additive character `u ↦ ω^{tr[⟨u, v⟩]}` on `F^m`. -/
   150	noncomputable def ffVecChar (v : Fin m → F) : AddChar (Fin m → F) ℂ :=
   151	  (ffChar (p := p) (F := F)).compAddMonoidHom
   152	    { toFun := fun u => ffDotProduct u v
   153	      map_zero' := by simp [ffDotProduct]
   154	      map_add' := by
   155	        intro u w
   156	        simp [ffDotProduct, add_mul, Finset.sum_add_distrib] }
   157	
   158	omit [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] in
   159	@[simp] theorem ffVecChar_apply (u v : Fin m → F) :
   160	    ffVecChar (p := p) (F := F) v u =
   161	      ffChar (p := p) (F := F) (ffDotProduct u v) :=
   162	  rfl
   163	
   164	omit [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] in
   165	private theorem ffVecChar_ne_zero [Finite F] {v : Fin m → F} (hv : v ≠ 0) :
   166	    ffVecChar (p := p) (F := F) v ≠ 0 := by
   167	  rw [AddChar.ne_zero_iff]
   168	  obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ : ∃ i, v i ≠ 0 := by
   169	    simpa [funext_iff] using hv
   170	  obtain ⟨b, hb0⟩ :=
   171	    ffTrace_nondegenerate (p := p) (F := F) (a := v i) hi
   172	  have hb : ffTrace (p := p) (F := F) (b * v i) ≠ 0 := by
   173	    simpa [mul_comm] using hb0
   174	  refine ⟨Pi.single i b, ?_⟩
   175	  have hdot : ffDotProduct (Pi.single i b) v = b * v i := by
   176	    unfold ffDotProduct
   177	    rw [Finset.sum_eq_single i]
   178	    · simp
   179	    · intro j _ hji
   180	      simp [hji]
   181	    · intro hi
   182	      exact (hi (by simp)).elim
   183	  rw [ffVecChar_apply, hdot, ffChar_apply]
   184	  intro h
   185	  exact hb ((AddChar.IsPrimitive.zmod_char_eq_one_iff p (ZMod.isPrimitive_stdAddChar p) _).mp h)
   186	
   187	/-- Paper label `prop:fourier-fact-vector`.
   188	
   189	The vector version of Fourier orthogonality: the expectation of the additive
   190	character `ω^{tr[⟨u, v⟩]}` over `u ∈ F^m` equals `1` when `v = 0`
   191	and `0` otherwise. -/
   192	theorem fourier_fact_vector (v : Fin m → F) :
   193	    𝔼 u : (Fin m → F), ffVecChar (p := p) (F := F) v u =
   194	      if v = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 := by
   195	  calc
   196	    𝔼 u : (Fin m → F), ffVecChar (p := p) (F := F) v u =
   197	        if ffVecChar (p := p) (F := F) v = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 :=
   198	      AddChar.expect_eq_ite _
   199	    _ = if v = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 := by
   200	      by_cases hv : v = 0
   201	      · have hzero :
   202	            ffVecChar (p := p) (F := F) v = 0 := by
   203	          subst v
   204	          ext u
   205	          simp [ffVecChar, ffDotProduct]
   206	        rw [if_pos hzero, if_pos hv]
   207	      · have hvc : ffVecChar (p := p) (F := F) v ≠ 0 :=
   208	          ffVecChar_ne_zero (p := p) (F := F) hv
   209	        simp [hv, hvc]
   210	
   211	end Vector
   212	end Fourier

   214	end MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries

     3	/-!

     5	
     6	The Pauli basis test uses fields of size `2^k` for odd `k`, together with a
     7	chosen self-dual normal basis over `ZMod 2`.  This file records that choice as
     8	data, while exposing Mathlib's basis and algebra-trace APIs for later proofs.
     9	
    10	## References
    11

    13	`def:subfield-trace`, and `def:binary-representation` in
    14	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:182-232` and `298-315`.
    15	Their paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:433-502,653-728`.

    18	open scoped BigOperators

    20	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

    22	/-- `IsAdmissibleSize q` is the predicate `q = 2^k` for an odd exponent.
    23	This is `def:admissible-size` in the blueprint
    24	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:210-212`, with paper origin
    25	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:662-667`.
    26	-/
    27	def IsAdmissibleSize (q : ℕ) : Prop := ∃ k : ℕ, Odd k ∧ q = 2 ^ k
    28	
    29	/--
    30	A fixed finite-field model records the carrier and the chosen coding of its
    31	elements by `Fin q`.  The algebra structure and stored basis data make explicit
    32	the paper's once-and-for-all self-dual normal-basis convention; they are
    33	deliberately part of the model rather than quantified afresh by the soundness
    34	theorem.  This is the Lean carrier for `def:binary-representation`, blueprint
    35	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:298-315`, paper origin
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:653-728`.
    37	-/
    38	/- The finite-field carrier is specialized to `Type 0`, as are the finite
    39	models used by the surrounding Euclidean-space API. -/
    40	structure FixedFieldModel (q : ℕ) extends MIPStarRE.LDT.FieldModel.{0} q where
    41	  /-- Scalar restriction from `ZMod 2` to the chosen field. -/
    42	  algebra : Algebra (ZMod 2) K
    43	  /-- Dimension of the chosen basis over the prime subfield. -/
    44	  basisDim : ℕ
    45	  /-- The chosen basis dimension is odd, as required for a self-dual normal basis
    46	  over the binary field. -/
    47	  basisDimOdd : Odd basisDim
    48	  /-- The admissible field-size relation for the chosen basis dimension. -/
    49	  basisCard : q = 2 ^ basisDim
    50	  /-- The chosen basis of `K` over `ZMod 2`. -/
    51	  basis : Module.Basis (Fin basisDim) (ZMod 2) K
    52	  /--
    53	  The inherited coding of `K` is the natural binary encoding of the stored
    54	  basis coordinates.  This field records the source's `downsize` convention
    55	  rather than allowing an unrelated permutation of `Fin q`.  It is the
    56	  coordinate clause of `def:binary-representation` in
    57	  `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:298-315`, with paper origin
    58	  `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:669-680`.
    59	  -/
    60	  representation_natural :
    61	    ∀ v : Fin basisDim → ZMod 2,
    62	      (toFieldModel.equiv (basis.equivFun.symm v)).val =
    63	        ∑ i : Fin basisDim, if v i = 1 then 2 ^ i.1 else 0
    64	  /-- Self-duality of the chosen basis with respect to the field trace. -/
    65	  selfDual : ∀ i j, Algebra.trace (ZMod 2) K (basis i * basis j) =
    66	    if i = j then 1 else 0
    67	  /-- Normality of the chosen basis, recorded by a Frobenius generator. -/
    68	  normal : ∃ α : K, ∀ i, basis i = α ^ (2 ^ i.1)

    70	/-!
    71	The paper fixes the field representation and self-dual normal basis once for

    76	-/
    77	
    78	/-- An admissible binary field size admits the fixed self-dual normal model used

    80	`def:dual-self-dual-normal-basis` and `def:binary-representation`, blueprint
    81	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:234-246,298-315`, paper origin
    82	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:653-680,702-725`.
    83	
    84	The construction of the basis and its natural coding is deferred to the
    85	algebra stage; keeping it as a named theorem makes the proof obligation visible
    86	without adding a model hypothesis to the source-facing test statements.
    87	-/
    88	theorem exists_fixed_field_model (q : ℕ) (hq : IsAdmissibleSize q) :
    89	    Nonempty (FixedFieldModel q) := by

     5	/-!
     6	# Subspaces for the Pauli basis test
     7	
     8	This module supplies the register subspaces, dot-product orthogonals, and the
     9	canonical coordinate complement used by the conditionally linear maps.  The
    10	canonical complement is presented through the intrinsic pivot-rank test; the
    11	equivalence with a particular row-reduced-echelon implementation is a later
    12	construction theorem.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The statement-level definitions are `def:register-subspace`,
    17	`def:dot-product-orthogonal`, `def:canonical-complement`, and
    18	`def:cl-canonical` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex`;
    19	the paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:231-384`.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	open scoped BigOperators
    23	
    24	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    25	
    26	variable {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    27	
    28	/--
    29	`registerSubmodule K S` is the span of the standard coordinate vectors indexed
    30	by `S`.  It is the Lean encoding of `def:register-subspace` from
    31	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:24-29`, whose paper origin is
    32	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:231-239`.
    33	-/
    34	def registerSubmodule (K : Type*) [Field K] (S : Finset ι) : Submodule K (ι → K) :=
    35	  Submodule.span K {v | ∃ i, i ∈ S ∧ v = Pi.single i 1}
    36	
    37	/--
    38	`dotOrthogonal W` consists of vectors whose coordinate dot product with every
    39	member of `W` vanishes.  This is `def:dot-product-orthogonal` in
    40	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:31-42`, with paper origin
    41	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:241-255`.
    42	-/
    43	def dotOrthogonal (W : Submodule K (ι → K)) : Submodule K (ι → K) where
    44	  carrier := {u | ∀ v, v ∈ W → dotProduct u v = 0}
    45	  zero_mem' := by
    46	    intro v hv
    47	    simp [dotProduct]
    48	  add_mem' := by
    49	    intro u v hu hv w hw
    50	    calc
    51	      dotProduct (u + v) w =
    52	          (dotProduct u w) + (dotProduct v w) := by
    53	            change (∑ i, (u i + v i) * w i) =
    54	              (∑ i, u i * w i) + (∑ i, v i * w i)
    55	            simp_rw [add_mul]
    56	            rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    57	      _ = 0 := by rw [hu w hw, hv w hw, add_zero]
    58	  smul_mem' := by
    59	    intro c u hu v hv
    60	    calc
    61	      dotProduct (c • u) v = c * dotProduct u v := by
    62	        simp [dotProduct, smul_eq_mul, mul_assoc, Finset.mul_sum]
    63	      _ = 0 := by rw [hu v hv, mul_zero]
    64	
    65	/-- Restrict a coordinate vector to the first `k` coordinates.  Lean-only rank
    66	infrastructure for `def:canonical-complement`, blueprint
    67	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:84-110`, paper `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:231-384`.
    68	-/
    69	private def prefixMap (k n : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ n) :
    70	    (Fin n → K) →ₗ[K] (Fin k → K) :=
    71	  { toFun := fun x i => x ⟨i.1, lt_of_lt_of_le i.2 hk⟩
    72	    map_add' := by
    73	      intro x y
    74	      rfl
    75	    map_smul' := by
    76	      intro c x
    77	      rfl }
    78	
    79	/-- The rank of a prefix restriction used by the pivot characterization. -/
    80	private noncomputable def prefixRank {n : ℕ} (W : Submodule K (Fin n → K))
    81	    (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ n) : ℕ :=
    82	  Module.finrank K (W.map (prefixMap k n hk))
    83	
    84	/--
    85	The non-pivot coordinate set of `W`, defined by the rank-increase
    86	characterization of pivots.  This is the basis-free encoding approved for
    87	`def:canonical-complement` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:84-110`;
    88	the paper's Gaussian-elimination presentation is
    89	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:303-320`.
    90	-/
    91	noncomputable def canonicalComplement {n : ℕ}
    92	    (W : Submodule K (Fin n → K)) : Finset (Fin n) :=
    93	  Finset.univ.filter fun j =>
    94	    prefixRank W (j.1 + 1) (Nat.succ_le_of_lt j.2) =
    95	      prefixRank W j.1 j.2.le
    96	
    97	/--
    98	The canonical coordinate complement spans a complement of `W`.  This is the
    99	proposition `lem:canonical-complement` in
   100	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:112-120`, with paper origin
   101	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:342-373`.
   102	The proof is intentionally deferred in the stage-4.1 skeleton.
   103	-/
   104	theorem isCompl_registerSubmodule_canonicalComplement {n : ℕ}
   105	    (W : Submodule K (Fin n → K)) :
   106	    IsCompl W (registerSubmodule K (canonicalComplement W)) := by
   107	  sorry
   108	
   109	/--
   110	The projector onto the canonical coordinate complement along `W`.  This is
   111	`def:cl-canonical` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:133-145`,
   112	originating at `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:375-384`.
   113	-/
   114	noncomputable def canonicalProjOfKernel {n : ℕ}
   115	    (W : Submodule K (Fin n → K)) : (Fin n → K) →ₗ[K] (Fin n → K) := by
   116	  let T := registerSubmodule K (canonicalComplement W)

1	\section{Conditionally Linear Functions, Distributions, and Samplers}
     2	\label{sec:linear}
     3	
     4	\subsection{Conditionally linear functions and distributions}
     5	\label{sec:cl}
     6	
     7	We first introduce \emph{conditionally linear functions}, which are used to
     8	specify the question distribution for games considered in the paper in a way
     9	that the question distribution can be ``introspected'', as described in
    10	Section~\ref{sec:introspection}.
    11	Intuitively, a conditionally linear function takes as input an element
    12	$x\in V = \F^n$ for some $n\geq 0$, and applies linear maps $L_j$ sequentially
    13	on $x^{V_j}$ where $V_1,V_2,\ldots $ are a sequence of complementary register
    14	subspaces such that both the linear maps $L_j$ and the subspace $V_j$ for
    15	$j \ge 2$ may depend on the values taken by previous linear maps $L_1(x^{V_1})$,
    16	$L_2(x^{V_2})$, etc.
    17	
    18	In the remainder of the section we use $V$ to denote the linear space $\F^n$ for
    19	some integer $n \geq 0$.
    20	For ease of notation we extensively use the subscript range notation.
    21	For example, if $V_1, V_2, \ldots, V_\ell$ are fixed subspaces of $V$ and $k \in
    22	\{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ we write
    23	\begin{equation*}
    24	  V_{<k} = \bigoplus_{j\,:\,1 \le j<k} V_j\;,\quad
    25	  V_{> k} = \bigoplus_{j\,:\, \ell\ge j > k} V_j\;,
    26	\end{equation*}
    27	and it is understood that $V_{\le k}$ and $V_{\ge k}$ are identical to
    28	$V_{<k+1}$ and $V_{>k-1}$, respectively.
    29	Moreover, if $V'$ is a register subspace of $V$, $F: V' \to V'$ is a function,
    30	and $x \in V$, we write $x^F$ to denote $F(x^{V'})$.
    31	For example, in the following definition $x^{L_1}$ is used as shorthand notation
    32	for $L_1(x^{V_1})$.
    33	
    34	
    35	\begin{definition}
    36	  \label{def:cl-func}
    37		Let $V$ be $\F^n$ for some $n\geq 0$.
    38	  For all integers $\ell\geq 0$ the collection of \emph{$\ell$-level
    39	    conditionally linear functions} (implicitly, \emph{on $V$}) is defined
    40	  inductively as follows.
    41	  \begin{enumerate}
    42	  \item There is a single $0$-level conditionally linear function, which is the
    43	    $0$ function on $V$.
    44	
    45	  \item Let $\ell \geq 1$ and suppose the collection of $(\ell-1)$-level
    46	    conditionally linear functions has been defined.
    47	    The collection of $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions on $V$ consists
    48	    of all functions $L$ on $V$ that can be expressed in the following form.
    49	    There exist complementary register subspaces $V_1$ and $V_{>1}$ of $V$, a
    50	    linear function $L_1$ on $V_1$, and for all $v \in L_1(V_1)$, an
    51	    $(\ell-1)$-level conditionally linear function $L_{>1,\, v}$ on $V_{>1}$,
    52	    such that for all $x\in V$,
    53	    \begin{equation*}
    54	      L(x) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}} (x^{V_{>1}})\;.
    55	    \end{equation*}
    56	  \end{enumerate}
    57	\end{definition}
    58	
    59	The concept of conditionally linear functions is simple even though the
    60	notations seem complicated.
    61	It is best understood using an operational definition illustrated in
    62	\cref{fig:cl-functions}.
    63	We give an example of a $2$-level CL function in \cref{ex:cl-function}.
    64	
    65	\begin{remark}
    66	  \label{rk:level-1-is-linear}
    67	  It follows from the above definition that all $1$-level CL functions are linear.
    68	\end{remark}
    69	
    70	\begin{example}\label{ex:cl-function}
    71	Consider $V = \F_{2}^{3}$. Then the following map
    72	\begin{equation*}
    73	  L:(x_{0}, x_{1}, x_{2})
    74	  \mapsto (0, x_{0}x_{2} + x_{1}x_{2} + x_{0},  x_{2})
    75	\end{equation*}
    76	on $V$ is a $2$-level CL function by choosing $V_{1} = \mathrm{span}\{(0,0,1)\}$, $L_{1}$
    77	the identity function on $V_{1}$, $V_{2} = V_{1}^{\perp}$, and
    78	\begin{equation*}
    79	  L_{2,\, x_{2}}: (x_{0}, x_{1}, 0)
    80	  \mapsto (0, x_{0}x_{2} + x_{1}x_{2} + x_{0}, 0),
    81	\end{equation*}
    82	which is linear for all $x_{2} \in \F_{2}$.
    83	Note that intuitively the function $L$ selects either $x_{0}$ or $x_{1}$ in the
    84	second coordinate conditioning on the value of $x_{2}$.
    85	\end{example}
    86	
    87	\begin{figure}[!htbp]
    88	  \centering
    89	  \begin{tikzpicture}
    90	
    91	
    92	
    93	    \node[draw, minimum width=2cm, anchor=east] at (0,0) (xv1) {$x^{V_{1}}$};

    96	    \draw[-stealth] (xv1.south) -- ++(0,-1) node[above right] {$L_{1}$} -- (xl1.north);
    97	
    98	    \node[draw, minimum width=2cm, anchor=west] at (0,-3) (xv2) {$x^{V_{2}}$};

   101	    \node[draw, minimum width=2cm, anchor=west] at (0,-5) (xl2) {$x^{L_{2}}$};

   106

   110

   112	  \caption{An illustration of an $\ell$-level CL function $L$.
   113	    First a register subspace $V_{1}$ and a linear map $L_{1}$ are chosen and
   114	    applied to obtain $x^{L_{1}} = L_{1}(x^{V_{1}}) \in V_{1}$.
   115	    Then depending the value of $x^{L_{1}}$, a register subspace $V_{2}$ and a

   120	\end{figure}
   121	
   122	\begin{remark}
   123	  \label{rk:higher-level}
   124	  Note that for any integer $\ell\geq 1$ the collection of $\ell$-level CL
   125	  functions trivially contains the collection of $(\ell-1)$-level CL functions:
   126	  for this it suffices to note that the $0$ function, which is a $0$-level CL
   127	  function, is also a $1$-level CL function by setting $V_1=V$, $V_{>1}= \{0\}$,
   128	  $L_1(x)=0$ for all $x\in V$, and $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ is the $0$ map for all
   129	  $x\in V$.
   130	\end{remark}
   131	
   132	\begin{definition}
   133	  \label{def:cl-dist}
   134	  Let $L, R: V \to V$ be conditionally linear functions.
   135	  The \emph{conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L,R}$ corresponding to $(L,
   136	    R)$} is defined as the distribution over pairs $(L(x), R(x)) \in V \times V$
   137	  for $x$ drawn uniformly at random from $V$.
   138	\end{definition}
   139	
   140	Throughout the paper we abbreviate ``conditionally linear functions'' and
   141	``conditionally linear distributions'' as \emph{CL functions} and \emph{CL
   142	  distributions}, respectively.
   143	
   144	The following lemma elucidates structural properties of $\ell$-level CL
   145	functions.
   146	Recall that using our shorthand notation, $x^{L_{<k}}$ and $x^{L_k}$ in the
   147	lemma denote $L_{<k}(x)$ and $L_{k,u}(x^{V_{k,\, u}})$ where $u = L_{<k}(x)$.
   148	
   149	
   150	\begin{lemma}
   151	  \label{lem:cl-kth}
   152		Let $\ell \geq 1$ and $V = \F^n$ for some integer $n \geq 0$.
   153	  A function $L: V \to V$ is an $\ell$-level CL function if and only if the
   154	  following collection of functions and subspaces exists:
   155	  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
   156	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-marginal} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$, a
   157	    function $L_{\le k} : V \to V$ called the \emph{$k$-th marginal of $L$};
   158	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-space} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u
   159	    \in L_{<k} (V)$, a register subspace $V_{k,\, u}$ of $V$ called the
   160	    \emph{$k$-th factor space with prefix $u$};
   161	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-map} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u \in
   162	    L_{<k} (V)$, a linear map $L_{k,\, u} : V_{k,\, u} \to V_{k,\, u}$ called
   163	    the \emph{$k$-th linear map of $L$ with prefix $u$};
   164	  \end{enumerate}
   165	  such that the following conditions hold for all $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots,
   166	  \ell\}$.
   167	  \begin{enumerate}
   168	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-cl} $L_{\leq k}$ is a $k$-level CL function on $V$;
   169		\item \label{enu:cl-space-sum} $V = \bigoplus_{i = 1}^\ell V_{i,\,
   170	      x^{L_{<i}}}$ for all $x \in V$;
   171	\item \label{enu:cl-map-sum} $L_{\leq k}(x) = \sum_{i = 1}^{k} x^{L_i}$ for
   172	    all $x \in V$, where $L_i$ is shorthand notation for $L_{i,\,
   173	      x^{L_{<i}}}$;
   174	  \item \label{enu:cl-last-ell} $L = L_{\leq \ell}$.
   175	  \end{enumerate}
   176	  As in \cref{enu:cl-map-sum}, we sometimes use $V_k$ and $L_k$ to denote
   177	  $V_{k,\, u}$ and $L_{k,\, u}$ respectively, leaving the prefix $u$ implicit.
   178	\end{lemma}
   179	
   180	\begin{proof}
   181		We first prove the ``if'' direction: if there exist spaces and functions
   182	  satisfying the conditions in the lemma, the fact that $L$ is an $\ell$-level
   183	  CL function follows from \cref{enu:cl-k-cl,enu:cl-last-ell} of the lemma
   184	  statement.
   185	
   186	  We now prove the ``only if'' direction.
   187	  Given a CL function $L$ on $V$, we construct the $k$-th family of subspaces
   188	  and functions for all $k \in \{1, \ldots, \ell\}$ by induction on the level
   189	  $\ell$.
   190	  First consider the base case $\ell=1$.
   191	  Since $L_{<1} = 0$, we omit the mentioning of the prefix $u \in L_{<1}(V)$.
   192	  Define $L_{\leq 1} = L$, the factor space $V_1 = V$, and the linear map $L_1 =
   193	  L$.
   194	  It is straightforward to verify that the conditions in the lemma hold for
   195	  these choices of linear maps and spaces.
   196	  
   197	  Now, assume that the lemma holds for CL functions of level at most $\ell - 1$,
   198	  and we prove the lemma for $\ell$-level CL functions.
   199	  By definition, an $\ell$-level CL function $L$ can be written as
   200	  \begin{equation*}
   200	  \begin{equation*}
   201	  	L(x) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{V_{>1}})
   202	  \end{equation*}
   203	  for some linear map $L_1 : V_1 \to V_1$ and a family of $(\ell-1)$-level CL
   204	  functions
   205	  \begin{equation*}
   206	    \bigl \{ L_{>1,\, v} : V_{>1} \to V_{>1} \bigr \}_{\, v \in L_1(V_1)}
   207	  \end{equation*}
   208	  where $V_1$ and $V_{>1}$ are complementary register subspaces of $V$.
   209	  Next, using the inductive hypothesis on the $(\ell-1)$-level CL function
   210	  $L_{>1,\, v}$ we get that for all $v \in L_1(V_1)$ and all $k \in \{1, 2,
   211	  \ldots, \ell-1\}$ there exist $k$-th marginal functions $L'_{v,\, \le k}:
   212	  V_{>1} \to V_{>1}$, $k$-th factor spaces $V'_{v,\, k,\, u}$, and $k$-th linear
   213	  maps $L'_{v,\, k,\, u}$ of $L_{>1,\, v}$ with prefix $u \in L'_{v,\,
   214	    <k}(V_{>1})$ such that the conditions of the lemma for $L_{>1,\, v}$ hold.
   215	  
   216	  Define the marginal functions $L_{\le k} : V \to V$, factor spaces
   217	  $V_{k,\, u}$ and linear maps $L_{k,\, u}$ for $L$ as follows.
   218	  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
   219	  \item Define $L_{\le 1} = L_1$ and the first factor space to be $V_1$;
   220	  \item For all $k \in \{2, 3, \ldots, \ell\}$, define
   221	    \begin{equation}
   222	      \label{eq:cl-k-def}
   223	      L_{\le k}: x \mapsto x^{L_1} + L'_{x^{L_1},\, <k} (x^{V_{>1}})
   224	      \quad\text{for } x\in V;
   225	    \end{equation}
   226		\item For all $k \in \{2, 3, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u \in L_{< k}(V)$, define
   227	    $V_{k,\, u} = V'_{v,\, k-1,\, w}$ and $L_{k,\, u} = L'_{v,\, k-1,\, w}$
   228	    where $v = u^{V_1} \in L_{1}(V_{1})$ and $w = u^{V_{>1}} \in L'_{v,< k-1}(V_{> 1})$.
   229	  \end{enumerate}
   230	  We verify that the conditions of the lemma are satisfied.
   231	  Since $L'_{v,\, < k}$ is by assumption a $(k-1)$-level CL function on $V_{>
   232	    1}$, we get that $L_{\leq k}$ is a $k$-level CL function on $V$ from
   233	  \cref{eq:cl-k-def}, establishing \cref{enu:cl-k-cl}.
   234	  By the induction hypothesis, we have for all $v\in L_1(V_1)$ and $y \in
   235	  V_{>1}$,
   236	  \begin{equation}
   237	    \label{eq:cl-k-1}
   238	    V_{>1} = \bigoplus_{i=1}^{\ell-1}
   239	    V'_{\smash{v,\, i, \, y^{L'_{v,\, <i}}}},
   240	  \end{equation}
   241	  which implies that for all $x \in V$ and $v = x^{L_1}$,
   242	  \begin{equation*}
   243	    V = V_1 \oplus \Big ( \bigoplus_{i=1}^{\ell-1}
   244	    V'_{\smash{v,\, i, \, x^{L'_{v,\, <i}}}} \Big)
   245	    = V_1 \oplus \Big (\bigoplus_{i=2}^{\ell} V_{i,\, x^{L_{<i}}} \Big)
   246	    = \bigoplus_{i=1}^\ell V_{i,\, x^{L_{<i}}}\;.
   247	  \end{equation*}
   248	  The first equality follows from \cref{eq:cl-k-1} while the second and third
   249	  equalities follow from the definition of $V_{k,\, u}$.
   250	  This establishes \cref{enu:cl-space-sum}.
   251	
   252	  Next, we have that for all $x \in V$, $v = x^{L_1}$, and $k \in
   253	  \{1,2,\ldots,\ell\}$,
   254	  \begin{align}
   255	    \label{eq:cl-last-ell}
   256	    L_{\leq k}(x)
   257	    & = v + L'_{v,\, <k} (x^{V_{>1}}) \\
   258	    & = v + \sum_{i=1}^{k-1} x^{L'_{v,\, i}}
   259	    = \sum_{i = 1}^{k} x^{L_{i}}, \label{eq:cl-last-ell2}
   260	  \end{align}
   261	  where $L'_{v,\, i}$ is the $i$-th linear map of $L_{>1,\, v}$ with prefix
   262	  $L'_{v,\, <i}(x)$ and $L_i$ is the $i$-th linear map of $L$ with prefix
   263	  $L_{<i}(x)$.
   264	  The second equality follows from the inductive hypothesis applied to $L'_{v,\,
   265	    <k}$ and the third equality follows from the definition of $L_{i}$.
   266	  Line~\eqref{eq:cl-last-ell2} implies \cref{enu:cl-map-sum} of the lemma.
   267	  
   268	  Finally, \Cref{enu:cl-last-ell} follows from~\eqref{eq:cl-last-ell} where we
   269	  set $k = \ell$ and observe that $L'_{x^{L_1},\, \le \ell-1}$ is equal to
   270	  $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ by the inductive hypothesis.
   271	  This shows that $L_{\le k}$, $V_{k,\, u}$, and $L_{k,\, u}$ satisfy the
   272	  conditions of the lemma and completes the induction.
   273	\end{proof}
